_confidence: HIGH: source names both the registration body and its document outright. MEDIUM: inferred from surrounding context. LOW: too thin to rely on.
_rule: name where the claim is lodged, never who adjudicates it
_source: help.unhcr.org and rimap.unhcr.org, extracted verbatim then curated by hand; internal displacement from IOM DTM, Global Protection Cluster and IDMC

ABW.caveat: Coverage gap on documents, so v2 cannot be worded for Aruba. The first step is booking online, so v1 should not imply the first contact was a visit, though the interview itself is in person at DIMAS. The site is served in Spanish and English only, so the Papiamento and Dutch names people may actually use are unavailable. Spanish accents restored here, no name changed.
ABW.channel: an appointment is scheduled online through the DIMAS website and the interview is then held in person at DIMAS; people applying at the border or port of entry apply to a migration officer instead
ABW.doc_why: the only document named on the Aruba pages is the asylum application form, which is what an applicant fills in rather than what registration produces; no permit, card or certificate for asylum seekers or recognised refugees is named anywhere on the site
ABW.office: Department of Integration, Management and Admission of Foreigners (DIMAS)
ABW.office_local: Departamento de Integración, Manejo y Admisión de Extranjeros (DIMAS)
ABW.office_why: DIMAS is the only named body that receives asylum applications on Aruba and DIMAS is the acronym people use; the migration officer route at the border has no named office or address, so it cannot serve as a prompt

AFG.caveat: Most respondents in Afghanistan will have applied for protection in Pakistan or Iran, not in Afghanistan, so the PoR card and the term Gorizah carry the question rather than any Afghan office. v1 misfires for in-country applicants because the first step is an email to UNHCR. Lifetime recall hazard: the three Encashment Centres at Kabul, Jalalabad and Kandahar are closed and were replaced by the Reception Centers, so earlier returnees will name a facility that no longer exists. No IDP registration document is named anywhere in the source.
AFG.channel: by email first - foreigners seeking asylum are told to email UNHCR and are contacted later; reception at the ICON Compound in Kabul is Monday and Wednesday 08:30-12:30 only. Afghan returnees registered abroad, not in Afghanistan
AFG.doc_alt: Voluntary Repatriation Form (VRF) - فورم بازگشت داوطلبانه (VRF) - د داوطلبانه راستنېدنې فورم (VRF)
AFG.doc_pending: UNHCR refugee or asylum seeker certificate
AFG.doc_why: the PoR card, which respondents call Gorizah, is the document Afghan returnees actually applied for and is the strongest recall anchor, and the UNHCR certificate is what in-country registration produces; the tazkira and e-Tazkira are national identity documents and the VRF is a repatriation form issued in the country of asylum, so both are kept out of the main slots
AFG.office_why: UNHCR handles asylum registration in Afghanistan because no government asylum system is described anywhere in the source; the Population Registration Department and the NSIA office only process tazkira and civil documentation, and the Reception Centers at Torkham, Spin Boldak and Lashkargah receive returnees rather than protection claims

AIA.caveat: MAJOR MISFIRE CASE: the only channel printed is email, so v1 cannot be used at all - there is no office the respondent could have gone to, and asking about one would produce false negatives from people who did apply. UNHCR is the only name available and there is no in-country office to attach it to, so the prompt must name UNHCR without a place. No document is named, so v2 cannot be asked. The source note describing the email channel is cut off in the input and the follow-up step after the email should be recovered.
AIA.channel: by email only - no office to visit; no national asylum office and no in-country UNHCR office is named
AIA.doc_why: No document, certificate or card is named for Anguilla
AIA.office_why: The source routes Anguilla to the UNHCR page, i.e. UNHCR rather than the state processes asylum claims, and no other body is named

ALB.caveat: The document version cannot be fielded - both document columns are empty by necessity and the 2021 Law on Asylum on Refworld would have to be checked to name the asylum-seeker card and the refugee ID. No Albanian-language name is printed for any office either, so every name here is English only and needs translation and piloting before fielding. The Directorate name appears in both a short and a Tirana form, and the National Commission in a short and a full form
ALB.channel: in person - initial interview with the Border and Migration Police on arrival, then a written asylum application submitted to the Directorate for Asylum and Citizenship in Tirana
ALB.doc_why: No document is named: the source states only a generic right to identification documents and residence permits, and the remaining entries (status of asylum-seeker, refugee status, subsidiary protection status) are status names rather than documents a respondent would hold
ALB.office_why: the Directorate receives the written applications and conducts the interviews and the Border and Migration Police is the first contact point on arrival, whereas the National Commission on Asylum and Refugees only reviews denied decisions on appeal

ARG.caveat: Spanish names given verbatim with accents as printed in source. Co.Na.Re. is formally the status-determination commission, but its executive secretariat is the physical counter where claims are lodged and the acronym is what people say, so naming it is not the adjudicator misfire. No colloquial name is printed for the Documento Provisorio and no protection-specific certificate is named for recognised refugees.
ARG.channel: in person at the SECONARE office in Buenos Aires, at a local Dirección Nacional de Migraciones office elsewhere, or before the migration authority on arrival at a border post or airport
ARG.doc_why: the Documento Provisorio is the provisional identity document issued to applicants; recognised refugees receive residencia temporaria, while the DNI is excluded as a doc_refugee because it is the same national ID Argentine citizens hold and will not distinguish refugees
ARG.office_why: the claim is lodged in person at the Secretaría Ejecutiva de la Co.Na.Re., which applicants call simply Co.Na.Re.; DNM is the lodging point outside Buenos Aires and is the better name to use for respondents in the provinces

ARM.caveat: No Armenian-language name is printed for any office or document, so every name must be read out in English and the local fields are empty. The refugee-status document has no formal title in the source, so v2 cannot ask about recognition; only the asylum stage can be worded. MCS both receives and decides, so it is a registrar as well as an adjudicator and is safe to name. Police stations and border points are ordinary government windows rather than dedicated asylum offices, so a v1 prompt naming only MCS will miss people who lodged at a border or from detention.
ARM.channel: in person - at the MCS head office in Yerevan (Davtashen 4th district 17/10, also Tairov str. 14), at a police station, at a land or air border crossing point, or from a penitentiary institution
ARM.doc_alt: a document certifying the refugee status - the page gives it no formal title, issuer or validity
ARM.doc_why: the asylum-seeker ID card is what MCS issues on application, gives free movement and is handed back to MCS on decision, so it is exactly the registration product; the Convention Travel Document is a travel document and the refugee-status document is named only by a descriptive phrase that no respondent would recognise said aloud, so the refugee slot is empty
ARM.office: Migration and Citizenship Service (MCS) under the Ministry of Internal Affairs of the Republic of Armenia
office_alt: Bagratashen, Bavra, Gogavan, Ayrum, Meghri, Zvartnots airport, Shirak airport (border crossing points)
ARM.office_why: MCS is printed as the competent authority that receives asylum applications in person, and its two printed renderings are merged here; UNHCR Representation in Armenia is explicitly stated not to register claims, and Action Against Hunger, Mission Armenia, HEKS/EPER, the Armenian Red Cross Society, World Vision and the Public Defender Office provide assistance or legal aid rather than registration

ATG.caveat: Major misfire case for both versions - the only channel named is email, no in-country UNHCR office and no national asylum office is named, so the v1 phrase about going to an office is wrong here, and no document is named at all. Both versions need bespoke wording
ATG.channel: by email to UNHCR; no office in country
ATG.doc_why: No document of any kind is named for asylum seekers or recognised refugees, so v2 cannot be worded for this country
ATG.office_why: UNHCR and not the state processes asylum claims here, and no national asylum authority exists - the Immigration Act is a statute rather than an office and claims otherwise run through general immigration machinery

AUS.caveat: No bridging visa is named anywhere in the source although it is the normal onshore asylum-seeker status document, so doc_asylum falls back to ImmiCard, an identity card rather than a status document. ImmiCard comes from RIMAP, not the HELP page. The application channel is not stated, so how_applied could not be filled.
AUS.channel: not stated in source - the UNHCR page describes no application channel; visas are processed and granted by the government
AUS.doc_alt: Temporary Protection Visa (TPV) and Safe Haven Enterprise Visa (SHEV)
AUS.doc_why: ImmiCard is the identity card asylum-seekers without passports actually carry and RoS is the current permanent protection outcome; TPV and SHEV are kept as backups because they are what the pre-2023 cohort will recall, and Class XB, Global Special Humanitarian, Community Support and Split Family are resettlement or family programmes, not documents issued on recognition
AUS.office_why: Home Affairs is the only body named as handling asylum determinations and lodgements; the Australian Human Rights Commission and Commonwealth Ombudsman are complaint mechanisms, MARA is a register of paid migration agents, and UNHCR Canberra explicitly cannot assist

AUT.caveat: The refugee-side answer is weaker: the three-year Aufenthaltstitel is the only thing named as issued on recognition and it shares its name with ordinary residence permits, so v2 for refugees will not discriminate well. German names given verbatim as printed in source: Bundesamt für Fremdenwesen und Asyl, weiße Karte, Ausweis für Vertriebene, Erfassungsstellen.
AUT.channel: in person at any police station or with a police officer; Ukrainians at special reception centres (Erfassungsstellen)
AUT.doc_alt: ID Card for Displaced Persons (Ausweis für Vertriebene)
AUT.doc_why: the white card is the document issued on admission to the asylum procedure and its colour name is the strongest recall item available; the Konventionsreisepass is a travel document and the Meldezettel a residence registration slip
office_alt: Federal Office for Immigration and Asylum (BFA)
AUT.office_why: the page states applications must be submitted directly at the police station or with a police officer, so that is where the claim is lodged; the BFA is the runner-up because it only receives the data afterwards, interviews and decides, and the Federal Administrative Court hears appeals

AZE.caveat: No Azerbaijani or Russian name is printed for the office or for either document, so the prompt can only be given in English or in translation. The refugee document is named only in the plural descriptive form Refugee Identity Documents, with no singular or formal title printed. UNHCR ceased operations in Azerbaijan on 31 August 2025 and stopped providing assistance on 31 July 2025, so respondents who registered earlier may name UNHCR rather than the SMS, and that office no longer exists to be visited.
AZE.channel: in person at the State Migration Service, 202 Binagadi Highway, Binagadi district, Baku; call centre 919
AZE.doc_why: The Temporary Certificate is issued to applicants within 15 days of applying and the refugee identity document on approval, whereas the travel document is excluded as a travel document applied for after status is granted
AZE.office_why: The State Migration Service is where the application is submitted in person, whereas the Head of SMS and the administrative courts only hear appeals and the RSD Department is an internal eligibility unit rather than a counter the applicant attends

BDI.caveat: All names are printed in French only - no Kirundi or Swahili mirror exists despite both being widely spoken, so local-language wording must be verified before fielding. Preuve d'enregistrement is a descriptive phrase rather than a printed official title. Status determination interviews are held at the Cishemere and Makombé transit centres, so some respondents will recall a transit centre rather than an office. ONPRA's full name is printed with several word-order variants across pages
BDI.channel: in person - pre-screening at the migration police, then registration with ONPRA at CUCOR or a transit centre
BDI.doc_why: The preuve d'enregistrement is issued following ONPRA registration and the CIR on recognition; the attestation de perte de document is a police loss certificate, not a protection document
BDI.office: National Office for the Protection of Refugees and Stateless Persons (ONPRA)
office_alt: Centre Urbain de Conseils et d'Orientation des Réfugiés (CUCOR)
BDI.office_local: Office National de Protection des Réfugiés et des Apatrides (ONPRA)
BDI.office_why: ONPRA performs the registration and biometric enrolment in ProGres, whereas the CCER takes the first-instance status decision and the comité de recours hears appeals; CGM only conducts the pre-screening interview

BEL.caveat: v2 cannot be fielded for Belgium from this source: the source itself flags that no page prints the annexe 26, the attestation d'immatriculation, the carte orange or the certificat d'inscription, so the asylum-seeker and refugee document names must be obtained elsewhere before use. The office name must be switched by language region - Office des étrangers in French-speaking areas, Dienst Vreemdelingenzaken in Dutch-speaking areas - and no English name is printed. The Office des étrangers is also printed once as Office de l'immigration. Individual housing is managed by associations and communes, so a respondent may have been accommodated with no reception centre involved
BEL.channel: in person - applications for international protection must be lodged at the Office des étrangers / Dienst Vreemdelingenzaken; temporary protection is registered in person at the Centre d'enregistrement, 40 Place Victor Horta, 1060 Bruxelles, with no online portal mentioned
BEL.doc_why: No asylum-seeker or refugee status document is named on any fetched UNHCR Belgium page - the only document printed is documents de voyage for recognised refugees, which is excluded as a travel document, so every document field is deliberately empty
office_alt: Fedasil (Agence fédérale pour l'accueil des demandeurs d'asile)
Centre d'enregistrement, 40 Place Victor Horta, Bruxelles (temporary protection only)
BEL.office_local: Dienst Vreemdelingenzaken (Dutch name for the same body)
BEL.office_why: The Office des étrangers is printed as the body where the application for international protection must be lodged, whereas the CGRA/CGVS is the first-instance determining body that only conducts the hearing and decides, and the Conseil du contentieux des Étrangers / Raad voor Vreemdelingenbetwistingen only hears appeals

BFA.caveat: No asylum-seeker document is named in the source, so v2 cannot be asked about the application stage in Burkina Faso - only about the CIR issued after recognition. Under the procédure collective for Malian nationals the family presents together with no individual eligibility interview, so an individual-level did-you-apply question may be answered no by members registered through the head of household. No IDP registration body and no IDP document is named (CONASUR does not appear), so PDI respondents have nothing to recognise. CIR validity is not stated on any page.
BFA.channel: in person at the Secretariat permanent de la CONAREF, at the siege in Ouagadougou or the antennes at Dori, Djibo, Ouahigouya and Bobo-Dioulasso; Malian nationals present as a family group under the procedure collective
BFA.doc_why: The CIR is the only protection document named and is issued by ONI on recognition; no asylum-seeker attestation or receipt is named anywhere, the carnet de naissance, livret de famille and certificat de nationalité are documents the applicant brings rather than receives, and the titre de voyage is a travel document
BFA.office_why: CONAREF is the sole asylum authority and its permanent secretariat is where the applicant presents in person, whereas the Comité d'éligibilité only interviews, the Comité de recours only hears appeals and ONI merely prints the cards

BGD.caveat: Bangladesh has no formal asylum procedure and no asylum-seeker certificate exists, so doc_asylum is left empty; the Smart Card is the single joint registration document for the whole registered population (issued 2018-2020, new QR format since). The toll-free line 16670 is an appointment hotline, not an office.
BGD.channel: in person - appointment taken at a Registration Appointment Desk in the Camp-in-Charge office, then attend the assigned joint registration site
BGD.doc_why: the Smart Card is the individual identity card produced by the joint registration exercise; the SCOPE card is explicitly stated to be a WFP food card and not a registration document
BGD.office_why: the joint Government-UNHCR registration site is where applications are actually processed and new documentation issued; the RRRC approves and the CiC administers the camp but neither is the place of registration

BGR.caveat: No Bulgarian-language name is printed for the refugee card or the humanitarian status holder card, and no colloquial or colour name is printed for any Bulgarian document. Ukrainians under temporary protection follow a separate route where re-registration until 30 April 2026 may be done at Ministry of Interior regional directorates, so a question naming SAR would miss them. Detention centres (Busmantsi, Lyubimets) are not registration points.
BGR.channel: in person at a State Agency for Refugees registration centre; initial applications also taken by the Border Police at the border
BGR.doc_why: the registration card is issued within about three days of registering and authorises stay until the end of the procedure, and the refugee card is issued on a grant of status; the address card and temporary protection registration card belong to the separate Ukraine route
BGR.office_why: SAR is the agency people register with and its registration centres are the buildings they physically attend; the Ministry of Interior regional directorates only re-register temporary protection holders and are ordinary police offices, not the refugee authority

BHS.caveat: The UNHCR page names no office at all and only says to approach the government immigration authorities or the relevant asylum authority. The Bahamas lacks dedicated asylum or refugee legislation and the Refugee Administration Unit (established 2016) is the sole named body. No document field could be filled.
BHS.channel: in person with the government immigration authorities; no office, address or channel is named in the source
BHS.doc_why: No asylum-seeker or refugee document of any kind is named for the Bahamas in either source, so v2 cannot be worded
office_alt: Refugee Administration Unit within the Department of Immigration
BHS.office_why: A claimant approaches a general immigration counter, so the parent Department is the recognisable name; the Refugee Administration Unit sits inside it, comes from RIMAP only and never appears on the UNHCR page, so it is kept as a backup rather than the stem

BIH.caveat: Confirmed coverage gap on documents: beyond the Attestation the source names nothing for recognised refugees, so v2 can only ask about the asylum stage. The BiH help site offers no Bosnian, Croatian or Serbian version, so the only local-language term captured for the whole country is the partner name Vasa Prava and every document must be read out in English. No appeals body is named. Despite its title the Ministry of Human Rights and Refugees is described only for post-decision integration and nothing is said about 1990s-conflict displaced persons or IDPs.
BIH.channel: in person - the intention to seek asylum is expressed to the Border Police or at any of the 16 Service for Foreigners' Affairs offices across the country, which then refers the person onward
BIH.doc_alt: Attestation on Expressed Intent to Seek Asylum - the second printed English wording of the same document
BIH.doc_pending: Attestation of the Intention to Seek Asylum (AISA)
BIH.doc_why: the Attestation is the only protection document named on the BiH pages and its colloquial name White Paper is what respondents will actually say, so it carries the asylum slot; no asylum-seeker card, refugee identity card, travel document or validity period is printed anywhere, so the refugee slot is empty by necessity
office_alt: Sector for Asylum of the Ministry of Security
BIH.office_why: the SFA is the office people physically attend, has 16 locations countrywide and issues the Attestation, whereas the Sector for Asylum both registers the formal application and issues the decisions and is not described as a place applicants visit, the Border Police only refers people to the nearest SFA office, and Vasa Prava and the Ministry of Justice legal aid offices provide assistance rather than registration

BLR.caveat: A person granted complementary protection rather than refugee status receives a separate Certificate on Granting of Complementary Protection (свидетельство о предоставлении дополнительной защиты), not captured in the refugee fields. All routes are explicitly in person - no online or app channel. No colloquial or colour names printed. The umbrella term государственная миграционная служба has no English rendering in the source.
BLR.channel: in person only - at a department on citizenship and migration, or to Border Guards on arrival, or to police or the detention administration if detained
BLR.doc_alt: Certificate on Application for Asylum in Belarus
BLR.doc_pending: Certificate on Registration of Asylum Application in Belarus
BLR.doc_pending_local: свидетельство о регистрации ходатайства о предоставлении защиты / убежища в Беларуси
BLR.doc_why: Belarus issues two successive asylum-seeker certificates, one on lodging and one after the interview registers the application; the registration certificate is the one held during the procedure, while the vid na zhitelstvo and the travel document are excluded
BLR.office_why: the department on citizenship and migration is the office of the state migration service that the source says people approach in person to apply; the Border Guards and police are entry points that refer people on rather than the registration office

BLZ.caveat: No document is named for recognised refugees, so the refugee half of v2 cannot be worded. Applicants holding a passport received a stamp in it rather than a separate card and may not think of that as a document at all, so v2 should be phrased to allow for a stamp. The English mirror prints the singular Refugee Department against the plural Departamento de Refugiados in Spanish.
BLZ.channel: in person and directly at the Refugee Department in Belmopan
BLZ.doc_why: the asylum receipt is the provisional document issued at registration to applicants without a passport, and the asylum stamp is the same provisional proof for those who hold one; nothing at all is named for recognised refugees
BLZ.office_why: the source states applications must be submitted directly and in person at the Refugee Department in Belmopan, so that is the place people went; the Ministry of Immigration is offered only as a backup name people may use in speech, since it takes the final decision and receives appeals rather than registering, while the Comité de Elegibilidad para Refugiados reviews cases and the Human Rights Commission of Belize only assists with appeals

BMU.caveat: Major misfire case. Only the Caribbean routing note exists for Bermuda: the sole channel is email, there is no office to visit and no document is named, so v1 cannot be used as written and v2 cannot be worded at all. Both document columns are empty by necessity, not omission
BMU.channel: by email to UNHCR; no office in country
BMU.doc_why: No document of any kind is named in the source - the Bermuda entry carries a single office row and no document section
BMU.office_why: the country is routed to UNHCR rather than to the state, so UNHCR and not a national authority processes asylum claims; no national asylum office, government department or in-country UNHCR office is named

BOL.caveat: The cédula de Identidad para Extranjeros is the general foreigners identity card issued to other resident foreigners too, so it does not identify protection status on its own. No colloquial or colour name is printed for either document. Claims may also be lodged before police or military forces at borders and airports, a channel an office-based question will miss. Source strips Spanish accents; standard accents restored here, no name changed.
BOL.channel: in person; in La Paz the claim is lodged at the Secretaría Ejecutiva de la CONARE and elsewhere at the nearest DIGEMIG office, verbally or in writing; at borders and airports it may be lodged with the migration authority or with police or military forces, after which CONARE schedules an in-person interview
BOL.doc_pending: Documento Temporal de Solicitante de Refugio
BOL.doc_pending_local: Documento Temporal de Solicitante de Refugio
BOL.doc_why: the Documento Temporal de Solicitante de Refugio is issued on registration and carries work, residence, health and education rights, and the cédula de Identidad para Extranjeros is what SEGIP issues after recognition; no other document is named on the Bolivia pages
BOL.office_why: CONARE is formally the status determination commission, but its executive secretariat is the counter where claims are lodged in La Paz and CONARE is the acronym people say, so this is not the adjudicator misfire; DIGEMIG is the lodging point everywhere else and is the better name for respondents outside La Paz, while SEGIP only issues the card after recognition

BRA.caveat: Filing is substantially online in SISCONARE, so v1 misfires unless it allows for the online step before the Policia Federal appointment; protocolo is by far the most recognised term and beats the formal DPRNM title; the CRNM does not mention refugee status on its face, so recognised refugees may not identify it as a protection document
BRA.channel: hybrid - the claim is filed online in SISCONARE (a valid email address is required) and an appointment is then attended in person at the Policia Federal, which also issues the documents
BRA.doc_pending: Documento Provisorio de Registro Nacional Migratorio (DPRNM)
BRA.doc_pending_local: Documento Provisorio de Registro Nacional Migratorio (DPRNM)
BRA.doc_why: The DPRNM is issued by the Policia Federal at the moment the claim is registered and the CRNM on recognition, whereas the CPF and CTPS are general tax and work documents and the Passaporte para Estrangeiro is explicitly unavailable to applicants
BRA.office_why: The Policia Federal is where applicants physically go, at the border or anywhere in Brazilian territory, and it issues the protocolo and the CRNM, whereas CONARE only analyses cases and issues the final decision and the DPU only gives legal assistance

BRB.caveat: The v1 office wording cannot be used unchanged: the only channel given is email, followed up by the UNHCR office in Panama, so there is no office anyone visited. Barbados has not acceded to the 1951 Convention or its 1967 Protocol and has no domestic RSD legislation; claims are submitted through UNHCR upon government request and processed by UNHCR regional offices. Same routing applies to the other Caribbean territories listed on the same page
BRB.channel: by email to UNHCR; no office in country
BRB.doc_why: no certificate or card of any kind is named for Barbados in either source
BRB.office_why: UNHCR and not the state processes asylum claims, and no national asylum office and no in-country UNHCR office is named at all, so UNHCR is the only nameable body

BWA.caveat: KEY FINDING: no documentation at all is issued at the application stage, so v2 returns nothing for asylum-seekers in Botswana and only v1 can be used for them - empty here is the true answer, not missing data. Encampment means the place people recall is Dukwi camp rather than any town office, so v1 should allow the camp as an answer. Ration Cards are the most recognisable paper people hold at Dukwi but are an assistance document, not a status document, and are deliberately excluded. No Setswana wording is printed. The Refugees Act was repealed and re-enacted in 2024 with a four-tier RSD process, so respondents who registered earlier dealt with different bodies
BWA.channel: in person - the Ministry of Justice takes the initial declaration and interview, applicants then reside at Dukwi camp while awaiting a decision, and UNHCR registration activities take place at the UNHCR office at Dukwi on Wednesdays 2pm-5pm
BWA.doc_why: The page states verbatim that no documentation is issued at the application stage, so the asylum-seeker fields are empty; the Manifest is the proof of registration UNHCR issues and replaces at Dukwi, whereas the decision letter is a decision and the ration card is an assistance document
BWA.office_why: The Ministry of Justice handles the initial declaration and interview and UNHCR performs the registration activities at Dukwi, whereas the Refugee Advisory Committee only processes applications, the Commissioner for Refugees and the Botswana Refugees Committee only determine status, and the FCII holds rejected applicants pending return

CAN.caveat: No colloquial name for the Refugee Protection Claimant Document is printed in source, so none is offered. The refugee-side answer is weak: source names no document issued on a positive IRB decision in Canada, and Confirmation of Permanent Residence applies only to refugees resettled from abroad. Most in-country claims start online, so v1 misfires unless the respondent claimed at the border.
CAN.channel: online through the IRCC portal from inside Canada, or in person at an airport or land border with CBSA
CAN.doc_why: the Refugee Protection Claimant Document is issued on being found eligible to claim; no in-country recognition document is named, so the resettlement Confirmation of Permanent Residence is the nearest available and work permits, study permits and travel documents are excluded
CAN.office_why: IRCC receives and processes claims filed from inside Canada and CBSA initiates those made at the border; the Immigration and Refugee Board is the tribunal that decides afterwards and is not where a claim is lodged

CHE.caveat: No German, French or Italian names are captured (the advertised German mirror serves English), so the letter names must be read out as printed; people from Ukraine hold the S permit and register through the RegisterMe online platform, so v1 misfires for them; since 1 January 2024 all new registrations take place in Bern
CHE.channel: in person at a Federal Asylum Centre (Altstatten, Basel, Balerna-Novazzano, Bern, Boudry or Zurich) or at a Swiss border post or airport; people from Ukraine register online on the RegisterMe platform instead
CHE.doc_alt: S permit (protection status S) for people from Ukraine; F permit for temporarily admitted refugees
CHE.doc_why: The N permit is issued on lodging the asylum application and the B permit on recognition, whereas the C settlement permit follows ten years of residence and the return visa and refugee travel document are travel papers
CHE.office_why: The Federal Asylum Centres are the printed in-person application points and the place people actually attend, whereas SEM decides the claim - SEM runs the centres, so a reviewer may prefer the widely used SEM acronym - and the Federal Administrative Court only hears appeals

CHL.caveat: No colloquial or colour names are printed for Chilean documents and both protection documents are permits rather than named cards, so recognition when read aloud may be weak; respondents are far more likely to name the cedula, which is a general foreigner ID and would be a false positive
CHL.channel: in person only - SERMIG in Santiago (San Antonio 580, 8:00-12:00 Monday to Friday) or a Direccion Regional; the claim must be lodged within 7 dias habiles of entry; later residence steps are done online at tramites.extranjeria.gob.cl
CHL.doc_alt: permiso de residencia temporal (8 meses, issued on formalising the claim); Cedula de Identidad Chilena para Extranjeros (cedula)
CHL.doc_pending: visa temporal de solicitante de refugio
CHL.doc_pending_local: visa temporal de solicitante de refugio
CHL.doc_why: The visa temporal de solicitante de refugio is issued to the applicant while the procedure is under way and the Permiso de Residencia Definitiva on recognition, whereas the cedula is a general foreigner ID, the Estampado Electronico is a downloaded stamp and the documento de viaje is a travel paper
office_alt: Departamento de Refugio y Proteccion Internacional
CHL.office_why: SERMIG is the in-person lodging point marked IN PERSON ONLY on the source and Extranjeria is what people actually call it, whereas the Departamento de Refugio y Proteccion Internacional is an internal unit of SERMIG and the Registro Civil only issues the cedula afterwards

CHN.caveat: UNHCR uses email as its primary contact channel, so v1 must allow for a claim begun by email rather than at an office; a respondent may answer yes to any police prompt because of the 临时住宿登记表 residence registration, which has nothing to do with asylum; no Chinese names are printed for the cards themselves
CHN.channel: email is stated as the primary channel of contact with UNHCR, followed by attendance in person at the UNHCR office in Beijing (Mon/Wed/Fri 2-5pm); there is no government asylum office
CHN.doc_why: Both cards are issued by UNHCR - the asylum-seeker card on registration and the refugee card on recognition, when the asylum-seeker card is handed back - whereas the Registration Form of Temporary Residence is the general police residence form every foreigner holds and is not a protection document
CHN.office_why: UNHCR is the only body that registers asylum seekers in China and there is no government asylum office; the local police station appears only for the 24-hour residence registration and naming it would produce a false positive

COD.caveat: Local authorities may receive claims where the CNR is absent and UNHCR receives them in those areas, so v1 naming the CNR alone will miss those respondents. Two asylum-seeker attestations exist - the APC on submission and the attestation de demandeur d'asile after the interview - and a respondent may recall either. No colloquial, Lingala or Swahili wording is printed anywhere in the source. Registration and services in Camp de Lusenda and Site de Mulongwe are accessed inside the camp rather than at a town office
COD.channel: in person at the CNR within 30 days of arrival; local authorities can receive the application and forward it to the CNR, and claims are lodged with UNHCR where the CNR is absent locally
COD.doc_alt: Attestation de Prise de Contact (APC), issued on initial submission before the interview
COD.doc_recognised: Attestation de la Commission Nationale pour les réfugiés
COD.doc_recognised_local: Attestation de la Commission Nationale pour les réfugiés
COD.doc_why: The attestation de demandeur d'asile is issued after the registration interview and the attestation de la CNR is what a recognised refugee produces to prove status for livelihood and education assistance, whereas the document de voyage is a travel document for repatriation and the document d'identité is a generic phrase
office_alt: HCR (UNHCR) where the CNR is absent locally
Autorités locales (local authorities that receive and forward applications)
COD.office_why: The CNR is the state refugee agency where the application is lodged and the agent interview is held, whereas the Commission d'Éligibilité only takes the first-instance decision and the Commission des Recours and the Conseil d'État only hear appeals

COK.caveat: Genuinely thin data rather than a confirmed absence - unlike Uzbekistan no source states that no asylum system exists, only that nothing has been published. help.unhcr.org/pacific carries no country-specific text and directs people to the UNHCR Representation outside the country (Canberra), so neither version of the question can be fielded without new country research
COK.doc_why: no permit, certificate or card is named in any source for the Cook Islands
COK.office_why: no asylum authority or office of any kind is named: RIMAP node 42 lists only immigration rather than refugee legislation and its country context page is marked Content to be added

COL.caveat: v1 wording misfires: the claim is emailed, there is no refugee office to attend. Millions of Venezuelans hold a PPT under the ETPV rather than any refugee document, and PEP, PIP and PTP are closed historical permits still relevant to lifetime recall. Cedula de Extranjeria is the third step in the refugee sequence and is obtained in person.
COL.channel: online and by email - forms downloaded from the Cancilleria portal and emailed; no office visit; Venezuelan temporary-protection registration (RUMV) is also online
COL.doc_why: the salvoconducto SC-2 is issued while the refugee claim is pending and is the word people actually use; the Documento de Viaje is a travel document and the Cedula de Extranjeria is a foreigner ID issued only after the visa
COL.office_local: GIT Refugio del Ministerio de Relaciones Exteriores (MRE) de Colombia (Cancilleria)
COL.office_why: GIT Refugio of the Cancilleria is where the refugee claim is lodged; CONARE / the Advisory Commission for Determination of Refugee Status only advises on the decision and is never attended by the applicant

CRI.caveat: The appointment is obtained online through the Portal de citas web while the eligibility interview is in person, so v1 must distinguish booking from attending. Migracion is what people say but is generic enough to catch any migration-office visit, so pair it with the DGME acronym. Respondents documented before July 2024 may recall a separate permiso laboral or Carne provisional de permiso laboral, since abolished as a separate document. Both carne de solicitante de refugio and carne de solicitante de la condicion de refugio are printed and are the same card; carne alone is what respondents say and is too generic to prompt with on its own. The DIMEX costs USD 68 and its acronym expansion is not printed in the source, so it must not be invented.
CRI.channel: appointment booked online through the Portal de citas web at www.migracion.go.cr or by telephone 1311, then in person for the interview at the DGME offices in Uraca, San Jose
CRI.doc_alt: carne de persona refugiada (refugee identity card named on the employment page)
CRI.doc_pending: carne de solicitante de la condicion de refugio
CRI.doc_pending_local: carne de solicitante de la condicion de refugio
CRI.doc_why: The carne de solicitante is issued on initial filing and the DIMEX, described as the documento de identidad oficial, on approval of the claim; the permiso laboral and Carne provisional de permiso laboral are work permits and since July 2024 work permission is integrated into the asylum-seeker card itself
office_alt: Unidad de Refugio de la Direccion General de Migracion y Extranjeria (DGME)
CRI.office_local: Direccion General de Migracion y Extranjeria (DGME)
CRI.office_why: The DGME processes all asylum applications through its Unidad de Refugio and is the office people physically attend, and Migracion is the name said aloud, whereas the Portal de citas web is only the booking channel

CUB.caveat: RIMAP contradicts help.unhcr.org: RIMAP says individuals may apply through unnamed national immigration authorities, while the help site says UNHCR Havana registers. The 2024 category of humanitarian residents is a status, not a card. Cuba is not party to the 1951 Convention, and the certificate is not a state document, which may weaken recognition of it in v2.
CUB.channel: in person at the UNHCR office in Havana; no government asylum office exists
CUB.doc_why: the UNHCR certificate is the only document named and the source states plainly that it does not constitute an official identity document; no separate refugee document is named, so doc_refugee is left empty
office_alt: Office of the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) in Cuba
CUB.office_why: UNHCR registers and conducts RSD itself because Cuba has no formal national refugee recognition mechanism; the Cuban Red Cross is a partner and explicitly not a registration point, and the national immigration authorities are named only by RIMAP with no office identified

CUW.caveat: The question stem itself misfires here: there is no asylum procedure and no refugee status, only a request for protection under Article 3 of the European Convention on Human Rights, so a question worded around asylum or refugee status will not match the local process or vocabulary. v2 cannot be fielded at all. The site is served in Spanish rather than Dutch or Papiamentu, so no Dutch or Papiamentu wording is available for either name.
CUW.channel: in person - an Article 3 ECHR protection request is lodged with UVTG at Winston Churchill Road sin numero; Curacao has no asylum procedure at all
CUW.doc_why: no document, permit or card of any kind is named on the Curacao pages - the site states verbatim that Curacao has no asylum procedure and describes only an Article 3 ECHR protection request, so both slots are empty by necessity rather than by omission
CUW.office: Unit for Supervision and Control of Foreigners at the Border of the Curacao Police Force (UVTG)
CUW.office_local: Unidad de Supervision y Control de Fronteras de los Extranjeros de la Fuerza de Policia de Curazao (UVTG)
CUW.office_why: UVTG is the only body named as receiving a protection request and it is a police unit people physically attend; Human Rights Defense Curacao offers legal assistance with Article 3 requests but does not register them, so it is not offered as a backup

CYM.caveat: Major misfire case. The only instruction, shared with Jamaica, Montserrat and Turks and Caicos Islands, is to email UNHCR, so v1 cannot be used as written because there is no office to go to, and v2 cannot be worded at all. Both document fields are empty by necessity, not omission.
CYM.channel: by email to UNHCR; no office in country
CYM.doc_why: No document, validity period or legal basis is named for the Cayman Islands, so v2 cannot be worded
CYM.office_why: UNHCR is the only body named for the Cayman Islands and emailing it is the only channel printed; no government office, department or asylum authority is named at all

CYP.caveat: Reviewer decision point: Alien Book is the strongest recognition hook in the whole Cyprus file and could replace the Confirmation Letter if false positives from non-protection migrants are acceptable. doc_refugee left empty on purpose - the only things named for recognised refugees are a three-year Residence Permit (too generic), the ARC and the Convention Travel Document (a travel document). Confirmation of the Temporary Protection Decision is the equivalent paper for people from Ukraine. Pournara is the colloquial name of the First Reception Centre in Kokkinotrimithia. No Greek-language names are printed anywhere in the source
CYP.channel: in person at the district police immigration office or at an airport or seaport on arrival; registration completed at Pournara; temporary protection also online
CYP.doc_pending: Confirmation of Submission of an Application for International Protection
CYP.doc_why: the Confirmation of Submission is the protection-specific paper issued the moment a claim is lodged; the ARC, colloquially the Alien Book, has far higher recall but is issued to every registered foreigner including students and workers, so naming it would draw heavy false positives
CYP.office_why: the intention to apply is expressed at the district police immigration office and registration then happens at Pournara, whereas the Asylum Service is the determining authority and the International Protection Administrative Court only hears appeals

CZE.caveat: Registration body clearly named, documents almost entirely missing: the source names only a permanent residence permit for recognised refugees and a long-term residence permit for subsidiary protection, both rejected here as generic residence permits that would draw large false positives from ordinary migrants. OAMP is the Odbor azylové a migrační politiky (Department of Asylum and Migration Policy) and dočasná ochrana is the Czech term for the status the sticker carries. Ukrainian speakers say Регіональних центрів допомоги Україні for KACPU and візову наклейку про тимчасовий захист for the sticker. Reception and detention centres (Zastávka u Brna, Kostelec nad Orlicí, Havířov, Bělá - Jezová, Balková, Vyšní Lhoty) are named lodging places for asylum-seekers
CZE.channel: in person at KACPU for temporary protection; asylum lodged at a reception centre or detention facility; long-term permit online via ipc.gov.cz
CZE.doc_why: no asylum-seeker card and no refugee status card is named anywhere in the source; the only protection document named is the temporary protection visa sticker pasted in the passport, which is not an asylum-seeker or refugee document but is the one thing that population holds and recognises
CZE.office_why: KACPU are the purpose-built regional centres where the largest protection population physically lodged and registered, and everyone calls them KACPU; OAMP is the ministry department that decides and handles exceptional cases rather than the counter people queued at

DEU.caveat: Aufenthaltserlaubnis is the same name used for many residence purposes and covers recognised refugees, subsidiary protection and a national ban on removal at different validity periods, so respondents may not link it to protection status. A rejected applicant may hold a Duldung long after the claim ended and may answer about that instead. No colloquial or colour names are printed on the German mirror. Respondents admitted through resettlement or humanitarian admission received a visa from a German mission abroad and never visited an in-country registration office. Before 2016 the first document was the BÜMA, which is not named on these UNHCR pages
DEU.channel: in person - first registration with the police, an arrival centre or a reception centre, then the formal asylum application at BAMF by personal appointment issued through the reception or registration office, not walk-in
DEU.doc_alt: Proof of Arrival (Ankunftsnachweis), held from initial registration until the application is filed with BAMF
DEU.doc_pending: Temporary Residence Permit for Asylum Procedure
DEU.doc_why: The Aufenthaltsgestattung is issued on formal filing of the asylum application and the Aufenthaltserlaubnis on recognition, whereas the Ankunftsnachweis only covers the period before the application is filed and the Visum and the Niederlassungserlaubnis are not tied to the protection claim
DEU.office: Federal Office for Migration and Refugees (BAMF)
DEU.office_why: BAMF is the authority the asylum application is filed with and the name people say as an acronym, whereas the Ausländerbehörde only issues residence permits after protection has been granted and the arrival and reception centres carry out the data, photo and fingerprint registration that precedes the application

DJI.caveat: Registration is joint - ONARS delivers the attestations and the refugee identity cards in collaboration with UNHCR - so respondents may name either body and who_registers is recorded as BOTH. ONARS is printed in two spellings (Office National and Office Nationale d'Assistance aux Réfugiés et Sinistrés); the fullest correct form is kept. The appeals procedure before the CNR is printed as not yet implemented, so an appeal-stage question does not apply. The acronym CNE is printed with no expansion anywhere in the source. The asylum attestation is valid six months and renewable, so long-settled respondents may have renewed it many times.
DJI.channel: in person at ONARS in Haramous, Djibouti-ville, 09:00-17:00, or at a border post; asylum seekers must present within 30 days of entering Djibouti; the UNHCR office receives Wednesday mornings by appointment only
DJI.doc_alt: attestations de réfugié (French-only name printed for the refugee attestation, no English form given)
DJI.doc_why: The attestation de demandeur d'asile is issued on registration with biometrics recorded in BIMS and the carte d'identité de réfugié on recognition, whereas the acte de naissance, acte de mariage and certificats de divorce are civil documents issued by the Sous-Préfecture and the Qadi
office_alt: National Office for Refugee and Disaster Victim Assistance
DJI.office_local: Office National d'Assistance aux Réfugiés et Sinistrés (ONARS)
DJI.office_why: ONARS manages asylum with UNHCR support and is where the applicant presents in person, whereas the CNR is the appeals commission, the CNE only determines status and the Administrative Court is the final recourse

DMA.caveat: Both v1 and v2 misfire: the only channel given is email, there is no office to name, and no document name exists to insert. Dominica is party to the 1951 Convention and the 1967 Protocol but has no specific legal framework for refugee status determination. Needs a Caribbean regional check before fielding.
DMA.channel: by email; no national asylum office and no in-country UNHCR office
DMA.doc_why: no document, certificate or permit of any kind is named for Dominica in the source
DMA.office_why: the source routes this country to UNHCR, i.e. UNHCR and not the state processes asylum claims; no other body, office or address is named anywhere

DNK.caveat: The appeal to the Danish Refugee Appeals Board is AUTOMATIC - the person takes no step at all - so a did-you-do-something question returns a false negative at the appeal stage and appeal-stage cases must not be classified as non-applicants. Temporary protection is applied for online at forms.nyidanmark.dk, so v1 cannot be used unchanged for Ukrainians. No Danish-language name is printed for the Immigration Service (Udlændingestyrelsen does not appear) or for either document, and the asylum card is named only in the long descriptive form, which is awkward to say aloud. The refugee document is a generic-sounding temporary residence permit that respondents may not link to protection status. Decisions are sent by letter, not collected in person.
DNK.channel: in person, walk-in, at Reception Centre Sandholm; persons who already hold a residence permit apply at the police station in their district, or to police at the border or airport; temporary protection under the Special Act is applied for online at forms.nyidanmark.dk or by appointment with the Citizen Service
DNK.doc_pending: ID card confirming that you have filed an asylum application
DNK.doc_why: The asylum ID card is issued as a direct result of filing the application and the temporary residence permit is what refugee, subsidiary protection and temporary protected status are all issued as; no other protection document is named
DNK.office_why: Sandholm is the walk-in place where the asylum application is actually filed and the Danish Immigration Service is the body it is filed with, whereas the Danish Refugee Appeals Board only hears the appeal and is never attended to apply

DOM.caveat: The ONR is housed inside the DGM immigration building, so respondents are likely to say they went to Migracion rather than to a refugee office - test both names. The source prints two Spanish variants of the asylum-seeker certificate (constancia de solicitud de la condicion de refugiado / constancia de solicitante de asilo), merged here. No distinct refugee ID card is named, only a one-year renewable residence permit.
DOM.channel: in person at the ONR, which sits inside the Direccion General de Migracion building in Santo Domingo; the constancia is renewed at the ONR every 30 days
DOM.doc_pending_local: constancia de solicitud de la condicion de refugiado
DOM.doc_why: the constancia is the certificate handed over on lodging and renewed monthly at the ONR, and constancia is the word people use; the permiso de residencia is the only thing named as granted on recognition of refugee status
DOM.office_why: the ONR is the office stated to receive asylum applications; CONARE is the interinstitutional body that determines who benefits from refugee status and is never attended by the applicant

DZA.caveat: v1 wording misfires: the application is submitted by email and there is no office to attend. Respondents are far more likely to recognise HCR than UNHCR. Algeria has no comprehensive asylum legislation.
DZA.channel: by email to the UNHCR office in Algiers; no walk-in office, address or appointment system published
DZA.doc_pending_local: شهادة طالب لجوء / certificat de demandeur d'asile
DZA.doc_why: these are the only two documents named and both are issued by UNHCR on registration and on recognition respectively; Arabic and French forms of each are merged into one cell
DZA.office_why: UNHCR conducts registration and RSD under its mandate and seat agreement; BAPRA exists in Decree No. 63-274 but is dormant and naming it would produce false negatives

ECU.caveat: No colour or colloquial name is printed for the refugee visa. The constancia has only 10 days face validity, so older applicants may not recall holding it. A substantial share of claims are filed online through www.gob.ec, so v1 as worded will misfire for those respondents.
ECU.channel: in person at regional offices of the Ministry, or online through the www.gob.ec portal with the receipt returned by email
ECU.doc_why: the constancia is handed over on lodging the claim and the visa de proteccion internacional is the status granted on recognition; the MERCOSUR and Amparo visas and the VIRTE are regularisation routes outside the asylum system
office_alt: Unidades de Proteccion Internacional de las Coordinaciones Zonales
ECU.office_local: Ministerio de Relaciones Exteriores y Movilidad Humana
ECU.office_why: the Ministry (universally called the Cancilleria) receives and registers the claim; the Registro Civil only issues the cedula afterwards to people already recognised

EGY.caveat: Registration is UNHCR-only, so naming the Passports and Immigration Administration would capture the later residence-permit step and not the protection application. No Arabic rendering of the UNHCR name itself is printed on the Egypt pages, so org_best_local is left empty - the Arabic building name is given in org_backup1 instead. Asylum Law No. 164 of 2024 is listed on RIMAP and may move registration to a government body, so very recent applicants may describe a different office.
EGY.channel: in person at the UNHCR premises in 6th of October City, by appointment obtained through the Infoline 0231330000 or the online Registration Appointment Tool; new-registration appointments are given on Tuesdays only
EGY.doc_alt: asylum seeker certificate (white certificate) - شهادة طالب اللجوء (الورقة البيضاء), valid 6 months, issued before the Yellow Card
EGY.doc_why: the Yellow and Blue cards are what registration and recognition themselves produce and respondents name them by colour; the white certificate is the shorter-lived first-issue paper so it is held as backup, while the residence permit, the negative decision letter and the appeal request form are not protection cards
office_alt: 6th of October Main Building (مبنى 6 أكتوبر الرئيسي)
RSD Building at 44A street, 2nd proximity, 8th District, 6th October City
EGY.office_why: UNHCR is the sole registrar in Egypt and its 6th of October premises are how people refer to it; the Residence Office of the Passports and Immigration Administration in Abbasiya only issues residence permits after UNHCR registration, the Appeal/Reopening unit is an internal UNHCR review channel and the Infoline is a telephone line

ESP.caveat: No document issued on recognition of refugee status is named anywhere in the source, so doc_refugee is empty by necessity - only the status names Estatuto de Refugiado and Protección Subsidiaria are printed. Renewal appointments are online only, so a question about going to an office misfires for that step. CREADE is printed with two different expansions, Acogida in Barcelona and Atención in Madrid and Málaga, and is run by NGOs (ACCEM, CEAR, Cruz Roja) rather than by officials. All names are Spanish only; no English titles are printed
ESP.channel: in person - intent to apply lodged at a Policía Nacional station or comisaría, then formalised at the Oficina de Asilo y Refugio; the appointment and every Hoja Blanca renewal are booked online only at icp.administracionelectronica.gob.es (cita previa)
ESP.doc_alt: Tarjeta Roja (the red card held once the claim is admitted to processing)
ESP.doc_pending: Resguardo de Presentación de Solicitud de Protección Internacional
ESP.doc_pending_local: Resguardo de Presentación de Solicitud de Protección Internacional
ESP.doc_why: the Hoja Blanca is the white sheet issued when the application is lodged and the Tarjeta Roja the red card held while it is processed, so both colour names should be read out and both beat the formal titles; the manifestación de voluntad is only the recorded expression of intent, and the TIE and the autorización de residencia y trabajo belong to Ukrainian temporary protection
office_alt: Centro de Recepción, Atención y Derivación (CREADE)
ESP.office_why: OAR is the competent asylum office and the acronym is printed verbatim beside the full name, and the Policía Nacional station is where the intent to apply is first recorded, whereas the Oficina de Extranjería handles general residence matters and CEAR, ACCEM and Cruz Roja only run reception places

EST.caveat: Notice of acceptance is a generic descriptor rather than a named card, so v2 may not be recognised when said aloud, and no Estonian-language document names are printed; refugee status in Estonia carries a temporary 3-year residence permit which respondents may not think of as a protection document; respondents will recall going to a police station rather than to an immigration office
EST.channel: in person at a police station (no appointment needed) or to the border guard at any Estonian border point; temporary protection for people from Ukraine begins online through politsei.ee
EST.doc_alt: Residence card and Decision granting temporary protection, both on the Ukraine temporary-protection route
EST.doc_why: The notice of acceptance is what registration itself produces and the temporary residence permit is issued on the grant of refugee status, whereas the residence card and the temporary protection decision belong to the Ukraine route
EST.office_why: The Board is the competent authority and claims are physically lodged at its police stations and border points, whereas there is no dedicated asylum or migration office to name and the accommodation centre is given only as a generic term

ETH.caveat: No colloquial or colour name is printed for either card. Refugee ID card appears in three printed variants (Refugee ID document, Refugee Identity Document, and with/without Fayda number and QR code) and UNHCR separately issues Asylum Certificates and a UNHCR asylum-seeker registration card. Registration now requires an online or phone appointment first, so v1 alone understates the process.
ETH.channel: in person at the RRS registration centre; appointment booked online through the DRCS portal or by phone to the UNHCR Call Centre
ETH.doc_why: the asylum-seeker card and refugee ID card are what registration and recognition produce; the Fayda digital ID and pass permit are a national ID and a travel permission, and the Refugee Travel Document is excluded
ETH.office_why: RRS is the registration and status-determination authority people name by its acronym and physically attend; the Appeal Hearing Council only hears appeals and the DRCS portal is a booking tool, not a place

FIN.caveat: No Finnish or Swedish name is printed for any office or document - the source does not contain the string Maahanmuuttovirasto and the short name Migri appears only inside the URL migri.fi, so neither is recorded here; the everyday name Migri is very likely the strongest prompt and should be confirmed before fielding. The claim is lodged with the police or a border guard rather than at an immigration office, so v1 should name the police as an alternative. The temporary protection residence card arrives by post within 14 days, so no office visit is involved for Ukrainians. Land border crossing points with Russia remain closed
FIN.channel: in person - walk-in at a police station with no appointment if already in Finland, or with a border guard at any border crossing point, airport or seaport on entry
FIN.doc_alt: residence card (temporary protection, delivered by post)
FIN.doc_pending: certificate of applicant of international protection
FIN.doc_why: the certificate is issued by the registering authority at application and the residence permit follows a positive decision on refugee status or subsidiary protection, whereas the temporary protection residence card covers Ukrainians only and arrives by mail
FIN.office_why: the Finnish Immigration Service manages asylum applications and is the body the applicant deals with throughout, while the police and the border guard are where the claim is physically lodged, whereas the Administrative Court and Supreme Administrative Court only hear appeals and the Asylum Unit and Department of International Protection are internal units of the service that no applicant visits

FJI.caveat: Total data gap. RIMAP node 63 country context reads Content to be added and help.unhcr.org bundles Fiji into a regional Pacific page with no country-specific text; only asylum-category legal instruments are listed. who_registers is recorded as NONE because the source names no registrar, not because none exists - a Pacific regional check is needed before either v1 or v2 can be fielded here.
FJI.doc_why: no permit, certificate or document is named for Fiji in the source
FJI.office_why: no authority, office, reception point or body of any kind is named for Fiji in the source, so no organization can be chosen without inventing one

FRA.caveat: v2 cannot be fielded for France from this source: the document respondents actually hold, the attestation de demande d'asile, is not printed anywhere and must not be invented. v1 must be reworded because access is appointment-only through SPADA or Ofii rather than by walking into an office. OFPRA is the name most respondents will recognise, but they attended it for the interview and the decision, not to register, so a reviewer wanting maximum recognition should test OFPRA as a second prompt rather than as the stem.
FRA.channel: in person by appointment only - the appointment is obtained through SPADA, and people living in Paris and Ile-de-France must contact Ofii first; no walk-in registration is described
FRA.doc_alt: Allocation pour demandeurs d'asile (ADA) - an allowance delivered on a payment card issued by Ofii at registration ; permis de séjour, 4 years renewable, printed for beneficiaries of subsidiary protection
FRA.doc_why: no asylum-seeker or refugee document is printed - the source states explicitly that attestation de demande d'asile, ADA card, récépissé, carte de séjour pluriannuelle and carte de résident do not appear on these pages - so both slots are left empty rather than filled with the titre de voyage, which is a travel document, or with the generic-sounding permis de séjour, which any permit holder would claim
office_alt: First Reception Structure for Asylum Seekers (Structure de premier accueil des demandeurs d'asile, SPADA)
French Office for Immigration and Integration (Office français de l'immigration et de l'intégration, Ofii)
FRA.office_why: the GUDA is printed as the single window where the asylum claim is registered, whereas OFPRA only decides the claim and holds the personal interview, the CNDA only hears appeals against OFPRA decisions and the prefecture only issues the residence document after recognition; SPADA and Ofii are the appointment-making entry points and are kept as backups

FSM.caveat: Nothing is named, so v2 cannot be worded and v1 can only say UNHCR; the source note for this country is cut off mid-sentence at the Pacific help page address, and UNHCR is recorded here by read-across from the identically worded Vanuatu note rather than from an explicit Micronesia statement - a reviewer may prefer NONE
FSM.channel: no office in the country; the Pacific help page gives no country-specific text and directs people to UNHCR
FSM.doc_why: No permit, card, certificate or document name is printed for Micronesia on either source
FSM.office_why: No asylum authority, office or registration point is named on RIMAP or on help.unhcr.org - only a constitutional provision carries the asylum category and the country context page states Content to be added - so UNHCR is the only body that can be named at all

GBR.caveat: The source names no place where a claim is lodged, so v1 can only name the Home Office as an institution rather than an office visited; BRPs expired 31 December 2024 and were replaced by the digital eVisa, so anyone recognised after that holds no card at all and only earlier respondents will name a BRP; the BRP is a general immigration card, not protection-specific; UNHCR prints Asylum Registration Card although Application Registration Card is the widely used alternative
GBR.channel: not stated on the source - no application office, port, screening unit or channel is named for lodging an asylum claim
GBR.doc_why: The ARC is the card issued at asylum registration and the BRP was the card issued on a grant of status, whereas the Afghan and Ukraine schemes are resettlement routes, Appendix FM and Appendix Family Reunion are application routes and the UKVI account is a login
GBR.office_why: The Home Office is the only body printed as responsible for receiving and deciding asylum applications and is the name people actually say, whereas UKVI is named only for creating the online account that holds the eVisa

GEO.caveat: No refugee document exists in the source, so v2 has no refugee prompt for Georgia. No Georgian-language wording is printed for any office or document - the only Georgian text is the title of the Law on International Protection - so all local wording must be sourced before fielding. The submission point changed on 27 October 2025 from UNHCR to the Martkopi Reception Center, so respondents recalling an earlier application will name UNHCR, which matters for a lifetime-recall question. Applications lodged in writing through the border or patrol police or from detention involve no office visit at all
GEO.channel: in person - since 27 October 2025 applications and supporting documents must be submitted at the Martkopi Reception Center rather than at UNHCR; an application may also be submitted in writing through the border police, the patrol police or a penitentiary or detention facility, with no office visit
GEO.doc_why: The certificate of asylum-seeker is issued once the application is declared admissible and confirms lawful presence; no document is named for recognised refugees - refugee and subsidiary protection (formerly humanitarian status) are printed as status names, not as documents a person could hold
GEO.office: Migration Department of the Ministry of Internal Affairs
office_alt: UNHCR Representation (the submission point until 27 October 2025)
GEO.office_why: The Migration Department is where asylum applications are submitted in person, through its Division of the International Protection Issues at 16 Mikheil Gakhokidze Street and, since 27 October 2025, at the Martkopi Reception Center, whereas UNHCR is no longer a submission point, the Social Service Agency is a general cash-assistance window and World Vision is an implementing partner

GRC.caveat: The pink card colour name is the strongest prompt available and should be preferred over the formal title. The refugee document is only a residence permit, which sounds generic and may not be linked to refugee status by respondents; the same Greek name covers refugee status and subsidiary protection at different validity periods. The Greek name of the RAO is printed only in the plural
GRC.channel: in person at a Regional Asylum Office or Reception and Identification Centre
GRC.doc_alt: Special alien's requesting asylum card (ειδικό δελτίο αιτήσαντος άσυλο αλλοδαπού)
GRC.doc_why: The pink card is issued on full registration and the residence permit on recognition; the refugee travel document is excluded as a travel document
office_alt: Reception and Identification Centre (Κέντρο Υποδοχής και Ταυτοποίησης, ΚΥΤ)
GRC.office_why: RAOs are printed as competent to receive asylum applications and carry out full registration, whereas the Appeals Authority, the Independent Appeals Committee and the Administrative First Instance Court only review decisions already taken

GRD.caveat: Asylum and related protection needs are handled through general immigration regulations, with registration and interviews on an ad hoc basis; Grenada has not acceded to the 1951 Convention or the 1967 Protocol. The only channel given is email. Both v1 and v2 misfire: there is no office to attend and no document to name.
GRD.channel: by email, no office in country
GRD.doc_why: no document is named in the source
GRD.office_why: the country page routes claims to UNHCR rather than to the state; there is no national asylum office, and no in-country UNHCR office is named either, so UNHCR is named as an organisation and not as a place

GTM.caveat: All names are printed in Spanish only, so the English columns repeat the Spanish. Two refugee documents are printed (DPI-E and DPI Rojo) and the source does not say which supersedes the other - DPI Rojo is the colour name respondents are most likely to recognise. Work permits are applied for online through Plataforma PEX, but the asylum claim itself is lodged in person
GTM.channel: in person at the DRER office in Guatemala City
GTM.doc_alt: Documento Personal de Identidad Especial (DPI-E); constancia de estatuto de permanencia provisional
GTM.doc_pending: constancia de solicitud del estatuto de refugiado
GTM.doc_pending_local: constancia de solicitud del estatuto de refugiado
GTM.doc_recognised: Documento Personal de Identificación para Extranjeros Domiciliados
GTM.doc_recognised_local: Documento Personal de Identificación para Extranjeros Domiciliados
GTM.doc_why: The constancia de solicitud is the proof issued on lodging the claim and the DPI Rojo is the card recognised refugees hold; the permiso de trabajo and the Documento Especial de Viaje are work and travel documents and are excluded
GTM.office: Departamento de Reconocimiento de Estatus de Refugiado (DRER)
office_alt: Centros de Atención para Personas Migrantes y Refugiadas (CAPMiR)
GTM.office_local: Departamento de Reconocimiento de Estatus de Refugiado (DRER)
GTM.office_why: DRER is printed as the competent authority that receives applications in person at a named address, whereas MINTRAB and RENAP only issue work permits and identity cards after the fact and the PDH is a human rights ombudsman with a complaint line

HND.caveat: The source prints Spanish names only, with no English names for any Honduran office or document. No colloquial or colour name is printed for the Autorizacion de Permanencia Temporal, so only the formal title is available for v2.
HND.channel: in person at any INM delegation (land, sea or air) or at a CAMI centre; the decision is notified by telephone or email
HND.doc_why: The Autorizacion de Permanencia Temporal is issued after biometric registration and renewed until the case is resolved, and the carne is obtained on registration as a recognised refugee; documento de identificacion is excluded as a generic term with no specification
office_alt: Centro de Atención al Migrante Irregular (CAMI)
HND.office_why: INM is the maxima autoridad en materia migratoria and receives applications at any of its delegations; the Comision de Refugio only receives the case with a recommendation and the Secretaria General del INM only issues the resolution, so the applicant never attends either, and CONADEH and SEDH register nobody

HRV.caveat: No Croatian-language name is printed for the ministry (Ministarstvo unutarnjih poslova does not appear) or for either document, so the prompt can only be given in English or in translation. Protection is requested from the police, so prompting with police station would catch ordinary police contact and produce false positives. The only short form printed for the asylum card is ID, which is too generic to use as a prompt. The source note recording a widely-used colloquial name for the Zagreb reception centre is cut off in the input and should be recovered before fielding. The temporary protection page names no document, no office and no legal citation, referring users to a government site instead.
HRV.channel: in person - protection is requested immediately on entry at a border crossing, at a police station, from the first police officer seen, or at the Reception Centre for Foreigners; the residence permit is applied for at the local police station within 15 days of approval
HRV.doc_alt: official note (issued by the MOI confirming asylum-seeker status ahead of the identity card)
HRV.doc_why: The asylum seeker's identity card is issued within three days of registering and the residence permit (identity card) is the single document issued to persons granted asylum or subsidiary protection, whereas azil and supsidijarna zaštita are status terms rather than documents
office_alt: Reception Centre for asylum seekers in Zagreb
HRV.office_why: The Ministry of the Interior is the competent authority that registers the claim, runs the reception centres and issues the asylum seeker's identity card within three days, whereas the Welcome Center is an information point and the administrative court only hears appeals

HTI.caveat: Very thin coverage: source names no asylum authority, office, law, document or certificate for Haiti, only ratification of the 1951 Convention, its 1967 Protocol and the 1961 Statelessness Convention. The document names come from the regional Kreyol page rather than a Haiti page, so confirm before fielding. Kreyol accents stripped for TSV safety. Registration is by email, so v1 cannot be used unchanged.
HTI.channel: by email only; no national asylum office and no in-country UNHCR office is named
HTI.doc_why: no document is named on any Haiti-specific page, so these are carried over from the Haitian Creole version of the regional Caribbean site, which is the page written for this population
HTI.office_why: the country is routed to the UNHCR page, meaning UNHCR and not the state processes asylum claims; no government asylum authority is named in any source

HUN.caveat: No asylum-seeker card is named for the ordinary asylum procedure, so doc_asylum falls back to the humanitarian residence permit, which belongs to the temporary-protection route. The registration point for asylum is a Hungarian embassy abroad, so v1 as worded misfires for asylum applicants. Menekult, Oltalmazott and Befogadott are status labels, not cards.
HUN.channel: in person at any NDGAP client office, but asylum requires a declaration of intent lodged first at the Hungarian embassy in Kyiv or Belgrade before entry; temporary protection may also be lodged at a Kormanyablak
HUN.doc_alt: personal identity card (személyi igazolvány) issued to recognised refugees
HUN.doc_why: The temporary protection card is protection-specific and covers the dominant Hungarian caseload, whereas the személyi igazolvány given to recognised refugees is the same national ID every citizen holds and would draw false positives; the bilingual travel document and the declaration of intent are excluded as a travel document and an application form
office_alt: Embassy of Hungary in Kyiv or Belgrade
HUN.office_why: NDGAP client offices are where an application is lodged in person and OIF is the acronym Hungarians use; Balassagyarmat and Nyírbátor are reception and accommodation sites rather than places a person would say they applied

IDN.caveat: UNHCR-mandate context with no government registration at all, so a v1 naming any government office returns nothing and UNHCR is the only correct organization. The same UNHCR card is held by asylum-seekers and recognised refugees, so the asylum/refugee distinction may not be visible to respondents. Appointments are requested online through My Services or a Kobo form before any office visit, so v1 cannot be used unchanged. No Bahasa Indonesia names are printed on the fetched pages
IDN.channel: appointment requested online through the My Services portal or the Kobo online inquiry form, then in person at the UNHCR Reception Center in Jakarta; renewed documents are collected there or mailed by the Indonesian Post Office to people outside greater Jakarta
IDN.doc_alt: UNHCR identity document (card or certificate) as printed on the registration page; Certificate as printed on the renewal form
IDN.doc_why: The UNHCR Card is the identity document issued to newly registered asylum-seekers and the Status Confirmation Letter is issued on positive recognition, whereas the Loss Report is a police report and the bare Certificate is only the renewal form's own wording
office_alt: My Services (online self-service portal used to request a registration appointment)
IDN.office_why: Indonesia is not a party to the 1951 Convention, has no national asylum system and the government does not conduct refugee registration, so UNHCR registers and carries out RSD under its mandate; the National, Provincial and Regency/City Refugee Task Forces are coordination bodies with no RSD or registration role

IND.caveat: India has no government asylum procedure, so v1 must name UNHCR; the source prints the plural forms Asylum seeker cards and Refugee cards and no Hindi or other local-language names; children under 12 hold paper documents rather than cards and unaccompanied children's cards are valid one year
IND.channel: in person at a UNHCR registration centre in New Delhi or Hyderabad; appointments are booked and managed through the My Services online portal and renewals may be booked up to 90 days ahead
IND.doc_alt: UNHCR asylum seeker document; individual refugee certificates with photos for children under 12
IND.doc_why: The asylum seeker card and refugee card are what registration and recognition themselves produce, whereas the RSD appointment letter is only a summons and the paper documents with photos are the under-12 variants of the same cards
