IND.office_why: UNHCR registers asylum seekers and conducts RSD in India and no government body plays any part, so naming an immigration department would misfire; MARI is included only because it is named as the Hyderabad registration centre, while the other partners provide legal aid or counselling

IRL.caveat: No document issued on recognition of refugee status is named, so doc_refugee is empty - the IRP card is a general immigration registration card issued to permit holders including temporary protection beneficiaries. The abbreviation TRC is explicitly not printed in the source and must not be assumed. Two named Dublin premises are used: Timberlay House for single applicants and couples without children, Citywest for families with children, and both are how people refer to them
IRL.channel: in person at the International Protection Office premises in Dublin, or at a port of entry
IRL.doc_alt: Irish Residence Permit (IRP) card; Temporary Protection Letter for Ukraine beneficiaries
IRL.doc_why: The Temporary Residence Certificate is issued after the preliminary interview at the IPO; the IPO2 questionnaire, Appeal Form and Permission to Remain Review Form are forms rather than identity documents, and no document tied to recognition of refugee status is named
IRL.office_why: The IPO is where the claim is lodged and where the Temporary Residence Certificate is issued, whereas IPAT only hears appeals, the Minister for Justice takes the final decision and IPAS only provides accommodation

IRN.caveat: Source names no asylum-seeker card: the 2025 Movaqqat cards (numbered 1 to 4) are the closest registration document but did not exist for earlier registrations, so for lifetime recall v2 should use Amayesh or Hoviat. UNHCR explicitly does not register, decide status or issue documents in Iran.
IRN.channel: in person at the aliens office in the area of residence; some administrative registration via designated Kefalat centres
IRN.doc_why: Amayesh carries refugee status protection for the Afghan majority and Hoviat is its Iraqi equivalent; passport, family passport, shenasnameh and student visa are excluded as not protection documents
IRN.office: Bureau for Aliens and Foreign Immigrant Affairs (BAFIA)
office_alt: Center for Foreign Nationals and Immigrants Affairs
IRN.office_why: BAFIA is the body that registers and issues the cards, and the short form اداره اتباع is what Afghans actually say; law enforcement is a control body, not a registrar, and UNHCR explicitly does not register in Iran

IRQ.caveat: Documents differ by region - the PIC in the Kurdistan Region and the PC-MoI card in central and southern governorates - so the doc_refugee prompt should be switched by region. No Arabic name is printed for the UNHCR Certificate itself. Kurdish Sorani forms of the residency card are printed in the source for Sorani-speaking areas
IRQ.channel: online request via My Services Portal, then in person at a UNHCR appointment
IRQ.doc_alt: PC-MoI card (بطاقة اللجنة الدائمة) for the central and southern governorates
IRQ.doc_why: The UNHCR Certificate is what registration itself produces and the PIC follows recognition; the Kurdistan Residency Card is a general residency card for visitors and workers and is not tied to protection status
IRQ.office_why: The source states all refugees and asylum-seekers in Iraq must register with UNHCR and obtain a UNHCR Certificate; the Permanent Committee of Political Refugee Affairs only decides status and the Residency Directorate only issues residency papers afterwards

ISL.caveat: The source flags that the Icelandic name of the Directorate appears only inside a URL and never as printed text, so no Icelandic-language name is available for any office or document and translation will be needed before fielding. The refugee document is a plain residence permit whose name does not signal protection, so v2 is weak. Many people apply at a police station or at the airport rather than at any immigration office, so v1 should offer the police as an alternative.
ISL.channel: in person, walk-in without appointment at the Reykjavik reception centre; at any police station outside Reykjavik; or with a border guard at Keflavik Airport
ISL.doc_alt: residence permit based on collective protection
ISL.doc_pending: certificate of applicant of international protection
ISL.doc_why: the certificate is what an applicant holds during the procedure and the temporary residence permit is what a grant of refugee status produces; no other protection document is named
office_alt: reception centre for applicants for international protection
ISL.office_why: the Directorate of Immigration is the body applied to and it runs the walk-in reception centre where claims are lodged; its Asylum Unit only assesses and the Immigration Appeal Board only hears appeals

ISR.caveat: No Hebrew-language names are printed anywhere in the source, only Arabic; the common acronym for the Population, Immigration and Border Authority is not printed and must not be introduced. Bnei Brak is used for registration and renewal, Eilat for renewal and Lod for the RSD interview, and people do refer to the offices by town. The first step is online, so v1 covers only the in-person completion step.
ISR.channel: form obtained online at govforms.gov.il, then completed and registered in person at the Ministry of Interior office in Bnei Brak
ISR.doc_why: the 2(a)(5) is issued on a separate paper to registered applicants and the A/5 serves as the temporary Israeli identity card for recognised refugees; the RSD application form is filled in rather than issued and the birth certificate is a civil document
office_alt: Ministry of Interior office in Bnei Brak
ISR.office_why: the Ministry of Interior office (the Population, Immigration and Border Authority) in Bnei Brak is where the application is completed and registered; UNHCR Israel is explicitly an advocacy office that has not done RSD since 2009, and the Appeal Tribunal only hears refusals

ITA.caveat: The source prints no status-specific name for the asylum-seeker permit - validity is given by protection type but the formal Italian permit wording is never printed - so permesso di soggiorno is generic and will also be recognised by migrants with no protection claim; do not invent a status-specific wording. The ricevuta is printed only for the temporary protection route, so it is not confirmed for ordinary asylum applicants. Questura is the name said aloud and beats the English legal title.
ITA.channel: in person at the immigration office of the Questura, or at a border police station on arrival; temporary protection by appointment made directly with the Questura
ITA.doc_why: The ricevuta is the certificate handed over at registration and the permesso di soggiorno is what protection status is issued as, with validity set by protection type, whereas the titolo di viaggio is a travel document and the codice fiscale a tax number
ITA.office_why: The asylum application is lodged orally or in writing at the immigration office of the Questura, whereas the Commissioni Territoriali only evaluate the claim, the Prefettura and SAI handle housing and reception and the ASL is a health service

JAM.caveat: Neither version can be worded from this source: application is by email so there is no office to visit, and no document exists to name; RIMAP records that there is no dedicated implementing legislation and that protection depends on administrative discretion, so many respondents will have no registration event at all
JAM.channel: by email to UNHCR - the only instruction printed for Jamaica (with the Cayman Islands, Montserrat and Turks and Caicos Islands) is to email UNHCR; no office, address or telephone number is named
JAM.doc_why: No document, card or certificate is named for Jamaica on either source, so no term can be offered without inventing one
JAM.office_why: The only body named for Jamaica on either source is UNHCR, contacted by email; no government office, department, committee or authority is named on help.unhcr.org or on RIMAP

JOR.caveat: UNHCR registers and the MoI card is collected at a police station, so a single-organization prompt captures only one of the two steps and the pair should be asked separately. No UNHCR refugee certificate is named - the asylum document covers both the asylum-seeker and the recognised stage, so doc_refugee holds the government card instead. الهوية الأمنية is printed as the colloquial for the Syrian-community variant of the MoI card (بطاقة الخدمة الخاصة بالجالية السورية في الأردن) and may not be used by non-Syrians. The Irbid and Mafraq registration offices have closed, so long-registered respondents may name an office that no longer exists. UNHCR documents are valid one year and need annual renewal.
JOR.channel: in person at a UNHCR registration centre, appointments arranged through the UNHCR Helpline; the MOI Service Card is issued separately at a police station
JOR.doc_alt: Proof of Registration (PoR), issued to each family in the camps
JOR.doc_why: The UNHCR Asylum Document is issued to each adult on completing registration and the MOI Service Card is the government card obtained afterwards, so the two stages stay distinct; Proof of Registration is camp-only
JOR.office_why: UNHCR runs the registration centres where the claim is lodged and issues the asylum document, whereas the Ministry of Interior only issues the service card afterwards through police stations and the UNHCR Helpline is a phone line rather than a place

JPN.caveat: Document version of the question cannot be fielded in Japan from this source - every document field is deliberately empty. HELP states UNHCR in Japan issues no refugee certificate or other document. No Japanese-script name is printed for the ISA or the Regional Immigration Services Bureau; the only Japanese-script office name available is UNHCR駐日事務所 and 難民支援協会 (JAR)
JPN.channel: in person at a Regional Immigration Services Bureau; the source does not state the application channel
JPN.doc_why: the source explicitly names no asylum-seeker ID card, no residence card and no certificate of refugee status; the Certificate of Eligibility for a Residency Status is for family members applying to join a recognised refugee, and JISR, RHEP and RVEP are study programmes, so nothing qualifies
JPN.office_why: the Regional Immigration Services Bureau is the office a person physically attends to make the application; the ISA is the national authority that decides recognition, and JAR is an NGO that only counsels and assists with the bureau application

KAZ.caveat: Key misfire: registration is done by the general employment and social programmes office, not a dedicated asylum or migration office, so a v1 prompt naming an immigration office would return false negatives - it must name this office or describe it as the social programmes office. UNHCR must not be offered here: the regional page states verbatim that UNHCR offices in Central Asia do not register refugees, do not examine asylum applications and do not issue refugee documents, so respondents who visited the UNHCR Representation in Almaty were only counselled. With no refugee document named, v2 can only be asked about the asylum-seeker's certificate
KAZ.channel: in person at the regional or city Department of Employment and Social Programs, or with the Border Service at an official border crossing point within 5 calendar days of arrival (1 day after irregular entry)
KAZ.doc_why: the asylum-seeker's certificate is issued upon registration of the application and is the only document named in the source; no document issued on recognition of refugee status appears anywhere, so the refugee columns are left empty rather than filled with an invented certificate name
KAZ.office: Department of Employment and Social Programs
office_alt: Ministry of Labor and Social Protection of Population
KAZ.office_why: the Department of Employment and Social Programs is the body where the application is lodged and registered and is printed with street addresses in Astana, Almaty, Shymkent and Konaev, whereas the ministry is only the parent authority with no public counter and the Bureau for Human Rights and the Red Crescent are partners giving legal and material aid, not registration points

KEN.caveat: DRS was called the Refugee Affairs Secretariat (RAS) until the rename and both names are still printed on the live pages, so respondents recalling earlier registration will say RAS; Alien card is the historic name most refugees still use for the Refugee ID; no Swahili or Somali names are printed
KEN.channel: in person at a DRS office or at the Kakuma or Kalobeyei Reception Center; in Kakuma registration is done at Field Post 2 and RSD interviews at the Data and Processing Centre
KEN.doc_alt: Proof of Registration; waiting slip issued while the Refugee ID is processed
KEN.doc_why: The Asylum Seeker Pass is issued at registration and the Refugee ID after recognition, whereas the Movement Pass, Convention Travel Document, Work Permit and National ID are travel, work and civil documents and the Decision and Rejection Letters are outcomes rather than registration papers
KEN.office_why: DRS is printed as the primary registration authority and as the place where asylum applications are registered, whereas the Refugee Status Eligibility Panel and the Commissioner for Refugee Affairs only decide claims and the Refugee Appeals Board only hears appeals

KGZ.caveat: UNHCR explicitly does not register refugees, examine applications or issue documents in Central Asia, so UNHCR must not be named in v1 here. The asylum-seeker certificate has a long formal title with no printed short or colloquial form and must be renewed every three months. No Kyrgyz-language names are printed anywhere, only Russian and English
KGZ.channel: in person - the source directs applicants to register at their local Population Services Center, with status determination handled by the labour ministry
KGZ.doc_pending: Certificate of Registration of an Application for Refugee Status
KGZ.doc_pending_local: Свидетельство о регистрации ходатайства о предоставлении статуса беженца
KGZ.doc_why: These are the documents printed as issued on registration of the application and on grant of status; the refugee travel document is excluded because the source states it is still in development and not yet issued
KGZ.office: Ministry of Labour, Social Security and Migration (MLSSM)
office_alt: Department for Work with Repatriates (Kayrylman) and Refugees
KGZ.office_local: Министерство труда, социального обеспечения и миграции Кыргызской Республики (МТСОМ)
KGZ.office_why: MLSSM is the competent asylum authority, runs status determination through its refugee department and is where refugees re-register annually so respondents did physically attend it; the printed lodging point ЦОН is a general one-stop civil-service centre used by the whole population and naming it would generate false positives - a reviewer wanting the literal lodging point should swap in the backup

KIR.caveat: The body appears only in the title of an instrument (Immigration Procedures Certified under the Immigration Act 2019), not as a place people attend; no registration channel, document, validity period or UNHCR presence is given. The name should be tested locally before v1 is fielded, and v2 cannot be built at all.
KIR.doc_why: no document is named in the source
KIR.office: Kiribati Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Immigration
KIR.office_why: the only body named for the country, taken verbatim from the title of the certified immigration procedures; the source never describes a registration counter, so this is the immigration authority rather than a confirmed place of lodgement

KNA.caveat: Major misfire case: there is no office to go to, so v1 cannot be used unchanged, and no document exists in the source for v2. The source states no domestic statute or administrative asylum procedure exists and that the decision is taken in another country, Washington. Both document fields are empty by necessity, not omission.
KNA.channel: by email to UNHCR; no national asylum office and no in-country UNHCR office is named, claims are referred to the UNHCR Honorary Liaison and are adjudicated by the regional office in Washington
KNA.doc_why: no document, card, certificate or validity period is named for Saint Kitts and Nevis, so v2 cannot be worded
office_alt: UNHCR Honorary Liaison in Saint Kitts and Nevis
KNA.office_why: UNHCR and not the state processes asylum claims here and emailing UNHCR is the only channel printed; the Honorary Liaison is the sole in-country presence named, but it is a referral point rather than an office people attend

KOR.caveat: No Korean-language names are printed on the source, so every name here is English only and cannot be read aloud to a Korean-speaking respondent as printed - a translation check is needed before fielding. Humanitarian status holders have no named card, only the status label.
KOR.channel: in person at a local immigration office; at the airport by expressing intent at immigration inspection; the application form is also available online via HiKorea
KOR.doc_why: the receipt is what the source states turns a person into a refugee status applicant, whereas the Application for Refugee Status Recognition is the form they fill in and the Notice on Non-Recognition is a rejection letter
KOR.office_why: the local immigration office is where the application form is obtained, submitted and receipted (source prints local immigration offices); the Ministry of Justice only decides appeals and 1345 is an information hotline

LBN.caveat: UNHCR registration of Syrians has been suspended since 5 May 2015 until further notice, so Syrians cannot obtain a registration certificate and most Syrian respondents hold papers issued before that date or none at all - decisive for a lifetime-recall question, which must accept registration that happened years ago. Reception centres in Tyre, Tripoli and Zahleh closed on 1 September 2025 with appointments consolidated in Beirut, so earlier registrants recall a different centre. No formal Arabic title is printed for either certificate; ورقة الأمم is the only Arabic document name available
LBN.channel: in person at the UNHCR reception centre in Beirut, admission only with a pre-scheduled appointment requested by phone through the contact centre or at a Khadamaty self-service machine
LBN.doc_why: the registration certificate is what registration itself produces and the refugee certificate follows UNHCR RSD, while exit certificates from Syria are Syrian exit papers rather than protection documents; ورقة الأمم (the UN paper) is printed as the colloquial name covering UNHCR papers generally and is the term respondents actually use
office_alt: reception centers in Tyre, Tripoli and Zahleh (closed 1 September 2025)
LBN.office_local: مركز الاستقبال التابع للمفوضية في بيروت
LBN.office_why: UNHCR conducts registration and RSD under its own mandate and the reception centre is the place people physically attend, whereas the UNHCR contact center is only a telephone appointment line and the Khadamaty machines only request an appointment

LBY.caveat: Registration starts on a phone or WhatsApp hotline rather than at an office, so v1 must allow for calling; no document name is published so v2 has no term to use; the Arabic name of UNHCR is printed on the source but is cut off in this extract, so no Arabic organization name is recorded here; many respondents will have been held in DCIM detention, where UNHCR does not register
LBY.channel: by telephone or WhatsApp to the UNHCR registration hotline, which then gives an appointment to meet UNHCR staff in Tripoli or another UNHCR registration location; people released from detention are given a registration appointment on release
LBY.doc_why: No certificate or card name is published on any Libya registration, protection, legal aid or announcements page in either English or Arabic, so v2 cannot be worded without inventing a name that does not exist on the source
LBY.office_why: Registration of asylum seekers in Libya is processed by UNHCR through its registration hotline, whereas DCIM only runs the detention centres UNHCR visits and does not register anyone, and Tawasul is a protection and family-tracing call centre

LCA.caveat: MAJOR MISFIRE CASE for v1: there is no office to visit, the only channel is email followed by referral to an Honorary Liaison, so the question must be reworded rather than have a name inserted. v2 cannot be used at all because no document is named. UNHCR is the right organization name but a respondent may never have entered a UNHCR office, since formal recognition and protection decisions are made by a regional office under UNHCR mandate rather than in country
LCA.channel: BY EMAIL - no national asylum office and no in-country UNHCR office is named; the only channel given is email, followed up through the UNHCR Honorary Liaison for the territory, with recognition decisions taken by a regional UNHCR office
LCA.doc_why: No asylum-seeker or refugee document is named on either source for Saint Lucia, so every document field is empty; the sources name only the referral route and the deciding regional office
LCA.office_why: UNHCR and not the state processes asylum claims in Saint Lucia and the UNHCR Honorary Liaison is the only named contact point; no national asylum office exists and no government body is named on either source

LIE.caveat: Organization side is solid, document side almost empty - the document version of the question can only be fielded for the Ukrainian population, using Status S. APA is the printed acronym for the Ausländer- und Passamt. Police lodgement matters here: outside office hours asylum requests go to the National Police, and temporary protection can be applied for at local police stations instead of the migration office
LIE.channel: in person at the office, at a border checkpoint, or at a police station outside office hours
LIE.doc_why: no asylum-seeker document and no refugee status document is named in the source; the only protection document named is Temporary Protection Status S, and even that is printed as a status label with no card name (no Ausweis S wording appears on the page fetched)
LIE.office_why: the Migration and Passport Office (APA) handles all asylum procedures and is also where people from Ukraine apply, whereas the Administrative Court only hears appeals and the Human Rights Association, Refugee Assistance and Chamber of Lawyers only advise or accommodate

LKA.caveat: The colloquial names carry this country: many respondents will only recognise asylum paper or refugee paper, and the source notes refugee paper is used loosely for both. No office name or address is printed for UNHCR Sri Lanka, so v1 is weak here and v2 is the stronger version. Sri Lanka is not party to the 1951 Convention and has no national asylum system.
LKA.channel: registration and status determination are with UNHCR only, reached by telephone 011-2580691 and by email, with no street address printed, so no office is named to go to; after registering with UNHCR it is mandatory to register at the local police station
LKA.doc_why: both certificates are the mandate RSD documents issued on registration and on recognition, and the source states they are commonly called asylum paper and refugee paper in Sri Lanka, which is the wording respondents will actually recognise
LKA.office_why: UNHCR is the only body that registers asylum seekers in Sri Lanka and the source states it is not possible to apply for refugee status with the Sri Lankan authorities; the local police station is a mandatory secondary registration after the UNHCR one, not an asylum application route, so naming it would capture the wrong event

LTU.caveat: No Lithuanian-language name appears anywhere in the source; the only local-language forms printed are Ukrainian, from the temporary protection mirror, so org_best_local is Ukrainian and not the language most applicants use. The refugee document is a plain permanent residence permit, not distinguishable by name from an ordinary permit, and the asylum certificate is described in descriptive words rather than by an official title, so v2 is weak here.
LTU.channel: in person, lodged with the border guard at any border point or at a border guard unit inside the country, or at the Migration Department; from Belarus at the Lithuanian embassy
LTU.doc_alt: certificate indicating that you have filed an asylum application
LTU.doc_why: both the registration card and the certificate are issued on filing an asylum application and the card is the more recognisable physical object to name; the permanent residence permit is what recognition produces, while the temporary residence permit belongs to subsidiary protection
office_alt: Embassy of the Republic of Lithuania in Belarus
LTU.office_why: applications are lodged either at the Migration Department or with the border guard, and the Migration Department is the more recognisable name, but many claims in Lithuania are in fact lodged at a border point, so the border guard backup is needed rather than optional

LUX.caveat: No product name is printed for the refugee document, only the generic descriptor residence permit valid for 5 years, so doc_refugee is weak and a reviewer should replace it if a proper name exists. Subsidiary protection is named as a status, not a document, and its holders do not receive the refugee travel document. The temporary protection certificate covers the Ukrainian cohort and is held as the backup. Grand Ducal Police and Grand-Ducal Police are the same body, merged to the hyphenated form.
LUX.channel: in person at the General Department of Immigration, where the application must be submitted personally; it may instead be lodged with the Grand-Ducal Police or with the control service at the airport, and people arriving from Ukraine register at the Ukraine Guichet Unique Enregistrement desk (12-14 avenue Emile Reuter, Thursdays, no appointment needed)
LUX.doc_why: the papier rose is the certificate issued three days after the claim is submitted and its colour name is what people actually say; the five-year residence permit is the only thing printed for recognised refugees, while the travel document for refugees, the explanatory leaflet and the form and appointment handed out at registration are all excluded
LUX.office_local: Direction générale de l'Immigration, Service des réfugiés
LUX.office_why: the application for international protection must be submitted in person to the General Department of Immigration, which is the registration point; the police are printed as an alternative lodgement channel and matter because a respondent may recall going to a police station rather than an immigration office, while the Ministry of Home Affairs appears only on the decision page as the parent ministry

LVA.caveat: The document names are generic descriptions rather than printed titles and no Latvian-language form or colloquial name appears anywhere in source, so v2 wording here is weak and should be verified locally before fielding. The temporary residence permit is what subsidiary (alternative status) beneficiaries receive; Ukrainians hold a separate residence permit based on temporary protection.
LVA.channel: in person to a border guard at any border point or at any State Border Guard office inside Latvia, no appointment needed; Ukrainians at OCMA territorial offices
LVA.doc_why: the asylum-seeker document is what the Border Guard issues to applicants who are not detained; no protection-specific certificate is named for recognised refugees, so the permanent residence permit issued on grant of refugee status is the best available
office_alt: Office of Citizenship and Migration Affairs (OCMA)
State Border Guard offices in Latvia
LVA.office_why: the page states asylum is applied for to a border guard at any border point or at any State Border Guard office in the country; OCMA is the runner-up because it only decides the claim after the Border Guard has registered it

MAR.caveat: Two-stage system: UNHCR registers and recognises, then the government BRA issues the national card, so v1 and v2 name different bodies at different stages and the wording should say UNHCR for the registration step. Arabic and French names are both printed and both in use; carte BRA is the colloquial form and is the strongest wording for v2. Renewal may happen at a temporary mobile location rather than a fixed office.
MAR.channel: in person at the UNHCR office in Rabat; renewals also at mobile UNHCR missions outside Rabat
MAR.doc_pending_local: شهادة طالب اللجوء / certificat de demandeur d'asile
MAR.doc_recognised_local: بطاقة اللاجئين الوطنية / carte nationale de réfugié
MAR.doc_why: the asylum-seeker certificate is issued by UNHCR on completing registration and the National Refugee Card by BRA on recognition; the Residency Card / carte de séjour is a general residence permit and is excluded
MAR.office_why: registration and RSD are conducted by UNHCR and not by the government; the BRA is visited only after UNHCR recognition, for a hearing and to collect the national refugee card, and the Inter-ministerial ad hoc Commission is an appeals/regularization body

MDA.caveat: The asylum and refugee documents are printed only as generic lowercase descriptions with no official title, no Romanian or Russian name and no colloquial form, so v2 wording needs local verification. Temporary protection registration begins online at protectietemporara.gov.md and requires a Moldovan address, so v1 cannot be used unchanged for that caseload. The Russian name of the inspectorate is Генеральная инспекция по вопросам миграции
MDA.channel: in person at the migration inspectorate, a border crossing point, a police office or a detention centre; temporary protection is registered online first then in person
MDA.doc_alt: temporary protection ID document (documentul de identitate al beneficiarului de protecție temporară)
MDA.doc_why: These are the only two documents the source ties to lodging an application and to recognition; the temporary protection card is a separate Ukraine-specific document held as backup
MDA.office_why: GIM (also printed IGM) is the migration inspectorate where applications are lodged and where the in-person temporary-protection appointment takes place; the Asylum and Integration Directorate is an internal unit of it and the Temporary Accommodation Centre is housing, not a registration point

MEX.caveat: Residencia Permanente is a general permanent residence card also issued on other grounds, so it does not identify protection status on its own, and no protection-specific refugee certificate is named in the source. COMAR offices printed: Ciudad de México, Tapachula, Palenque, Tenosique, Oluta, Guadalajara, Tijuana, Saltillo, Monterrey. Source strips Spanish accents; standard accents restored here, no name changed.
MEX.channel: in person at a COMAR office, or at an INM office where there is no COMAR office; the claim must be lodged within 30 working days of arrival
MEX.doc_alt: Tarjeta de Visitante por Razones Humanitarias (TVRH)
MEX.doc_why: the Constancia is the proof issued once the asylum procedure has begun and the Residencia Permanente is what INM issues on recognition; the CURP temporal is a population registry code rather than a protection document, and the TVRH is a humanitarian visitor card carrying work authorisation, so it is held as a backup rather than used as the main asylum prompt
MEX.office_local: Comisión Mexicana de Ayuda a Refugiados
MEX.office_why: COMAR is where the claim is lodged and is the acronym everyone uses; INM is the alternative filing point where no COMAR office exists and is the better prompt for respondents outside the nine COMAR cities, and Migración is what people call INM in speech

MHL.caveat: Nothing usable for either question version. Source carries only a constitutional provision under the asylum-rights category and the country context page states Content to be added. Both v1 and v2 need original field research or a regional Pacific source before this country can be worded.
MHL.doc_why: No permit, certificate or document name is printed in any source for this country
MHL.office_why: No asylum authority, office or registration body is named in any source; only a constitutional asylum-rights provision exists, with no dedicated refugee or asylum statute

MKD.caveat: Both document fields are empty because of an explicit coverage gap in the source, not because nothing is issued. No Macedonian-language names are printed for any office. The social ministry has been renamed from Ministry of Labour and Social Policy to Ministry of Social Policy, Demography and Youth and both names still appear on the site, so both may be recognised by respondents
MKD.channel: in person at the Sector for Asylum in Skopje
MKD.doc_why: Documented coverage gap - no source page names any card or document issued to asylum seekers, recognised refugees or subsidiary protection holders, so no document can be offered and v2 cannot be worded for this country without further research
MKD.office_why: The Sector for Asylum inside the Ministry of Interior is printed as the competent body conducting the first-instance asylum procedure and is the asylum office people attend, whereas the Centre for Social Work and the social ministry only handle integration plans and accommodation and the Tabanovce and Vinojug centres are transit facilities

MLT.caveat: org_best_local holds Identità, the separate agency that issues the residence permit after the IPA grants status - it is not the lodging point. The residence permit is shared with subsidiary protection beneficiaries so it does not identify refugee status on its own. The source prints the ASD name in two variants (Asylum Seeker Document / Asylum Seekers' Document), merged here. No Maltese-language document names printed.
MLT.channel: in person at the International Protection Agency, appointment requested by email; people in detention notify the Immigration Police or the Detention Services Agency
MLT.doc_why: the ASD is issued once the application is registered and is the document people carry to access services; the Convention Travel Document is a travel document and the residence permit is the only status document named for recognised refugees
MLT.office_why: the IPA is where the claim is registered and which issues the Asylum Seekers Document; the International Protection Appeals Tribunal only hears appeals and AWAS provides welfare and accommodation, not registration

MMR.caveat: Neither v1 nor v2 can be fielded in Myanmar without new source work. Do not substitute the citizenship scrutiny cards: the colour names Pink Card, Blue Card and Green Card are printed verbatim and would be strong recall prompts, but they are nationality documents and would produce false positives from the general population. The Household List is recorded as a backup only because it is the instrument that proves who lives where, the closest analogue available. Despite 3,509,780 IDPs recorded, no IDP registration, no IDP card and no camp management body is named.
MMR.channel: no application channel is named anywhere in the source - the only issuer wording is the generic phrase relevant authorities in Myanmar
MMR.doc_alt: Household List (အိမ်ထောင်စုလူဦးရေစာရင်း)
MMR.doc_why: The only documents named are the citizenship scrutiny cards (Pink, Blue and Green Card), a birth certificate and the Household List - all civil status or citizenship documents, none of them issued as a result of applying for protection
MMR.office_why: NO NAMED OFFICE: no ministry, township office, immigration office or camp management body is named anywhere in the source, and the generic phrase relevant authorities in Myanmar is not a name a respondent could recognise

MNE.caveat: No Montenegrin-language document names are printed anywhere and the document names above are the page's descriptive wording rather than formal titles, so none can be read aloud as-is without translation and shortening. A second, distinct certificate is issued after the application is lodged. Health Booklets for Refugees and IDPs is historical (2005).
MNE.channel: in person at the Directorate for Asylum in Podgorica (Mon-Fri 07:00-15:00); temporary protection strictly in person at the MoI branch office in the municipality of residence
MNE.doc_pending: certificate proving that you expressed an intention to seek asylum
MNE.doc_why: The intention certificate is the first document issued and the one that confers asylum-seeker status and legal residence; the Application for International Protection of a Foreign National is a form the applicant submits, and the refugee travel document is excluded as a travel document
MNE.office_why: The Directorate is the place with a public address and opening hours where applicants attend and Limenka is the building nickname printed on the page, which is the form people would recognise aloud; the Administrative Court is excluded as the appeals body

MNG.caveat: The entire country site is a single thin landing page: no street address, no walk-in office, no appointment system and no document name. Both v1 and v2 misfire here - there is nothing to attend and nothing to name - and this should be flagged rather than filled with a plausible-sounding office.
MNG.channel: by email only, no office in country
MNG.doc_why: no document of any kind is named in the source
MNG.office_why: UNHCR in Mongolia is the only named entity and the only access channel on the whole country site; no government asylum office is named at all

MSR.caveat: Major misfire case. Montserrat is routed to the local-government page but nothing is named there: no office, no department, no document and no legal basis, so v1 has no place to name and v2 has no document. Both document fields are empty by necessity, not omission. This matches the Cayman Islands and Turks and Caicos Islands rows, which carry the same email instruction.
MSR.channel: by email to UNHCR; no office in country
MSR.doc_why: no document, validity period or legal basis is named for Montserrat, so v2 cannot be worded
MSR.office_why: the only instruction printed for Montserrat, shared with the Cayman Islands, Jamaica and the Turks and Caicos Islands, is to email UNHCR; no government office, department or asylum authority is named at all

MYS.caveat: The UNHCR Card is tagged as issued to all registered persons rather than to recognised refugees specifically, so it is the single recognisable item for both groups. Since 9 April 2026 all new registration requests must be submitted online through My Services only, so v1 as worded misfires for recent registrants; the Appointment Card was discontinued at the end of 2019 but may still be recalled by long-registered respondents.
MYS.channel: online through the My Services portal (compulsory for new requests since April 2026), then in person at the UNHCR Reception Centre for the appointment
MYS.doc_why: the UNHCR card is the identity document issued on completing registration and is what everyone calls it; the Under Consideration letter covers those still pending, while the Individual and Registration Group Numbers are identifiers not documents
MYS.office_why: UNHCR is the only body that registers asylum seekers in Malaysia; no government department plays any part, so no immigration authority should be named

NER.caveat: Prima facie recognition matters for lifetime recall: Malians and Nigerians recognised as a group received an Attestation de réfugié and never attended an individual interview, so they may answer no to a question built around applying. Two printed names exist for the asylum-seeker attestation (Attestation de demande d'asile, Attestation provisoire) and two for the refugee card, and the site is French-only so no Hausa, Zarma, Kanuri or Tamasheq wording is available. Most refugees are in camps and zones d'accueil rather than at the Niamey Guichet Unique.
NER.channel: in person - at the Guichet Unique in Niamey for urban cases, or inside the camp or zone d'accueil elsewhere; the Ligne verte 0 800 12 12 is an enquiry line only
NER.doc_alt: Attestation de réfugié (Prima Facie), 1 an renouvelable, for Malians and Nigerians recognised as a group ; Attestation provisoire, 3 mois, the second printed name for the asylum-seeker attestation
NER.doc_why: the attestation issued by the CNE is what lodging produces and the Carte d'identité de réfugié - shortened on the rights page to Carte de réfugié - is what recognition produces, whereas the Titre de voyage de la Convention de Genève de 1951 is a travel document, the VRF is a repatriation form and the Attestation de protection temporaire covers only Nigerian arrivals
office_alt: Direction Générale de l'État Civil et des Réfugiés (DGEC-R)
NER.office_local: Guichet Unique de Protection et d'Assistance des refugies et demandeurs d'asile urbain
NER.office_why: the Guichet Unique is printed as the joint reception desk in Niamey where registration actually happens, with the CNE sitting inside it, whereas the Commission Nationale d'Éligibilité only deliberates on eligibility, the Ministère de l'Intérieur only signs the attestation and the Ligne verte is a toll-free telephone channel; DGEC-R runs the CNE secretariat and the camps are where registration is accessed outside Niamey

NGA.caveat: No local-language names are printed - Hausa, Yoruba, Igbo and Nigerian Pidgin wording must be verified before fielding - and no colloquial name or acronym is recorded for any document. Entry is through a generic immigration post before referral, so some respondents will recall immigration rather than NCFRMI. Respondents who registered before the 2022 rename will say National Commission for Refugees. Temporary Protection Status is listed among documents provided but is not described
NGA.channel: in person - the asylum seeker presents to the immigration authority at entry or on arrival and is referred to the nearest NCFRMI office; nine NCFRMI registration offices are listed and services are free
NGA.doc_alt: Proof of Registration (printed also as asylum seeker proof of registration); refugee registration card / identity card
NGA.doc_why: The asylum seeker certificate is issued on registration and is renewable for 6 months while RSD runs, and the Refugee Certificate follows recognition, whereas Convention travel documents, birth certificates and the National Identity Number are not protection documents
NGA.office: National Commission for Refugees, Migrants and Internally Displaced Persons (NCFRMI)
office_alt: National Commission for Refugees (name used before the 2022 rename)
NGA.office_why: NCFRMI receives and processes asylum applications and is named as the body that registers and issues documentation through its nine offices, whereas the Eligibility Committee only deliberates on status determination and the Refugee Appeal Board only hears appeals

NIU.caveat: Total data gap - neither v1 nor v2 can be worded from this source. who_registers is recorded as NONE because the source names no registrar, which is not evidence that no procedure exists. help.unhcr.org covers Niue only through a regional Pacific page with no country-specific text. A Pacific regional check or original country research is needed before fielding.
NIU.doc_why: no permit, certificate, card or document name is printed for Niue in any source
NIU.office_why: no authority, office, reception point or body of any kind is named for Niue - RIMAP node 132 carries only a constitutional provision under the asylum-rights category, with no dedicated refugee or asylum statute, and the country context page states Content to be added

NLD.caveat: Serious coverage gap on both halves: no application centre is named at all (no aanmeldcentrum appears in the source) and no protection document is named, so v2 cannot be worded and v1 has no confirmed office to name. The right answers are almost certainly absent from the file rather than non-existent, so this country should be re-scraped before fielding.
NLD.channel: the source names no walk-in application office: the IND is reachable by telephone 088 043 0430 or an online contact form at ind.nl, and the only in-person point printed is the info desk of the reception centre (AZC) staffed by COA; registration in the municipal records database after six months is an administrative act
NLD.doc_why: the only document term printed is verblijfsvergunning, the generic Dutch word for residence permit, which is not tied to protection status; the source states that no page fetched names the W-document, the vreemdelingenidentiteitsbewijs or any asylum residence permit, so no document could be chosen without inventing one
office_alt: Central Agency for the Reception of Asylum Seekers (COA)
NLD.office_why: the IND is the authority the application is made to and IND is the acronym people say, but the source explicitly warns it is not presented as a walk-in office, so COA and the AZC are given as backups because they are the places people physically attended; the Aliens Police is named only as the body asylum seekers report to regularly, and VluchtelingenWerk Nederland and RefugeeHelp.nl are NGO services rather than registration points

NOR.caveat: No Norwegian-language name is printed on any page fetched - the source states explicitly that asylsokerbevis does not appear - so org_best_local and both document local fields are empty and an interviewer would have to read English names aloud. No document is named for recognised refugees, so v2 cannot ask about refugee status. UDI is the acronym Norwegians actually say but it decides rather than registers, so a reviewer wanting recognition over accuracy may prefer it.
NOR.channel: in person - at the nearest police station if already in Norway, to the border police at the border, or at the Råde National Arrival Center since 15 July 2024, with applicants arranging and paying for their own transport
NOR.doc_alt: Residence Card issued after approval of temporary collective protection, valid one year and renewable annually
NOR.doc_why: the asylum-seeker card is issued on registration and its two printed spellings are merged here; the travel document provided by the Norwegian Authorities is a travel document, the D number and the National Identity Number are population identifiers rather than documents, and the Residence Card is generic in speech and covers only temporary collective protection, so it is held as a backup
NOR.office_why: NPIS is printed as the body that registers the applicant and takes fingerprints, photos and tuberculosis testing, whereas the Norwegian Directorate of Immigration (UDI) only processes the application and conducts the asylum interview and the Immigration Appeal Board (UNE) only hears appeals; the Råde arrival centre is the physical place people attended from July 2024 and any police station is where those already in the country present themselves

NRU.caveat: Nothing usable for either question version: RIMAP node 125 names dedicated refugee legislation but no office, no application channel and no document, and the country context reads 'Content to be added'. Both the organization and the document names must be sourced elsewhere before Nauru can be fielded. Note the offshore-processing history means many respondents in Nauru were processed under Australian arrangements, which are not described in this source
NRU.channel: NOT STATED - no application channel, office or contact point is named; RIMAP country context reads 'Content to be added'
NRU.doc_why: No permit, card or document is named for Nauru; Refugee Status, Derivative Status and Complementary Protection are the three protection categories named in the title of the 2019 Regulations, which are status categories and not documents a person could hold
NRU.office_why: No office of any kind is named for Nauru on RIMAP node 125 - the source names only the dedicated refugee legislation and the three protection categories, so there is no body to name in v1

NZL.caveat: Worst coverage in the batch: neither source names an RSD authority, an appeals body, an application channel or any document, so neither v1 nor v2 can be fielded for New Zealand from this file and both names must be sourced elsewhere before use. Immigration New Zealand, the Refugee Status Unit and the Immigration and Protection Tribunal are the bodies a reviewer would expect but none is printed, so none is recorded here. The resettlement programme for people transferred to Nauru and Papua New Guinea ran July 2022 to June 2025 and is closed
NZL.channel: NOT STATED - no application channel, office or appointment route is named on either source; the only government reference printed is the website immigration.govt.nz
NZL.doc_why: No document, card, permit or visa is named for New Zealand on help.unhcr.org/newzealand or in RIMAP node 128; the only entry printed under documents is the name of the closed Nauru and Papua New Guinea resettlement programme, which is a programme and not a document a person could hold
office_alt: immigration.govt.nz (web address only - no agency name is printed on any source)
NZL.office_why: No lodging or registration body is named on either source: the Immigration Advisers Authority is a regulator of immigration advisers and explicitly not the RSD authority, and the government immigration service is referenced only by its web address, so no name qualifies as an office a respondent went to

PAK.caveat: Source carries no statement that government registration is closed or frozen, but names no government registration office either, so BOTH rests on the PoR/ACC cards being government-issued. blue card is a second colloquial for PoR (blue cards issued April 2021). PCM centres closed early August 2025 and were repurposed as Voluntary Repatriation Centres; kept as a backup because the question covers a lifetime. VRC/reception centres and the TWIC letter are repatriation instruments, not protection registration
PAK.channel: by phone appointment with a UNHCR partner, no walk-ins; My Services portal online for updates
PAK.doc_why: the PoR card is what the registered Afghan population actually holds and says aloud, so it beats the UNHCR Refugee Card which covers only the small non-Afghan caseload; ACC is the backup for the large cohort that never obtained PoR
office_alt: Proof of Registration Card Modification (PCM) Center
PAK.office_why: UNHCR is the registrar for new asylum claims and the name every Afghan recognises; SHARP, SEHER and IMKAAN only take the appointment by phone on UNHCR's behalf, and no government registration office is named anywhere in the source

PAN.caveat: Applying by email is a named route for people already in the country, so v1 cannot be used unchanged. The asylum side runs through two cards in sequence - the ONPAR carnet on lodging and the SNM card once the claim is admitted a tramite - and respondents will call both simply carne, so the prompt should read out both. The 5 August 2025 rule making the ONPAR carnet the only valid asylum-seeker ID is recent, so lifetime recall spans older cards. No English document names are printed, the source strips accents from Spanish names, and ONPAR is rendered once as Oficina Nacional de Proteccion de Asilo y Refugio on the Spanish landing page
PAN.channel: MISFIRE - applicants already in Panama apply by email to ONPAR (protecciononpar@minseg.gob.pa) or in person at the ONPAR office in Condado del Rey; at borders and the airport they tell the first authority or an SNM official and ONPAR responds within 24 hours
PAN.doc_alt: carne que te identifica como solicitante admitido de la condicion de refugiado (issued by SNM once the claim is admitted a tramite, renewed every 6 months)

PAN.doc_pending_local: documento de identificacion valido como solicitante de la condicion de refugiado

PAN.doc_recognised_local: carne de permanencia temporal como refugiado
PAN.doc_why: the ONPAR carnet is issued on lodging and since 5 August 2025 is the only valid asylum-seeker identity document, and the carne de permanencia temporal is issued by SNM on recognition, whereas the refugee work permit is an employment document

PAN.office_local: Oficina Nacional para la Atencion de Refugiados (ONPAR)
PAN.office_why: ONPAR receives and processes the applications and is the acronym printed on the card people hold, whereas CONARE only evaluates cases and takes the final decision and the source states applicants do not lodge with it directly; SNM is the general migration service that issues the later cards, and MITRADEL is the labour ministry

PER.caveat: The Carné de Extranjería is the general foreigner card, also issued to Calidad Migratoria Humanitaria holders, so it does not identify protection status on its own. PER.doc_pending_local: Carné de solicitante de la condición de refugiado
PER.doc_why: the carné de solicitante is issued on registering and the Carné de Extranjería on recognition; the Autorización de Trabajo Virtual is a work permit and the Comisión Revisora forms are appeal material, both excluded
office_alt: Oficinas Desconcentradas (ODE) del Ministerio de Relaciones Exteriores
PER.office_why: the Espacios de Protección are the printed in-person filing points where the claim is actually lodged; the CEPR decides the claim at first instance and MIGRACIONES only issues the foreigner card, so neither is where the person went to register

PLW.caveat: Neither v1 nor v2 can be fielded in Palau. The absence is a source coverage gap rather than an established finding: the country context page states Content to be added, and no dedicated refugee or asylum statute is listed, only a constitutional provision. The Pacific regional page carries no per-country detail for Palau either. New source work is needed before this row can be used.

PLW.doc_why: No permit, certificate or document name is printed for Palau
PLW.office_why: No asylum authority, office or department is named - only a constitutional provision carrying the Asylum rights category, with the country context page marked Content to be added

PNG.caveat: No usable data. who_registers is recorded as GOVERNMENT because the source tags the entry as government and lists a dedicated National Refugee Policy (2015), not because any body is named - none is. There is no in-country UNHCR office and the country is covered from Canberra, so UNHCR is not the registrar either. Neither version of the question can be worded without new country research
PNG.doc_why: No permit or document name is printed anywhere in the source
