POL.caveat: Two completely separate routes: asylum-seekers go to the Border Guard, but the far larger population from Ukraine registered in person at the municipal office (Urząd Miasta / urząd gminy) for PESEL UKR and never met the Border Guard. PESEL UKR is strictly a personal identification number rather than a protection document, but it is the thing that population applied for and will name; residence card CUKR (karta pobytu CUKR) is the alternative and is applied for online only via the MOS portal, which the office-based question stem cannot capture. No Polish-language name is printed for the asylum-seeker certificate
POL.channel: in person at any Border Guard unit or at the border; also by post or e-mail; CUKR online only via the MOS portal
POL.doc_why: the temporary certificate of foreigner's identity is the document issued on lodging an asylum claim; the work permit document is excluded as a work permit, and no document is named for recognised refugees
POL.office_why: the Border Guard is where an application for international protection is lodged and registered; the Office for Foreigners only processes and decides it and the Refugee Board and Voivodeship Administrative Court only hear appeals

PRT.caveat: No Portuguese-language document names and no colloquial terms are printed, so both document names would have to be translated before fielding. Asylum can be lodged with any police force or at the border, so an AIMA-only office stem will miss those routes. EECIT is a detention centre, not a public office.
PRT.channel: in person at AIMA or a Loja AIMA branch, or to any police force (PSP, GNR, Maritime Police), or at an airport border post; Ukraine temporary protection online
PRT.doc_alt: temporary residence permit (6 months, renewable) issued on admission to the regular procedure
PRT.doc_pending: Declaration proving the submission of your application for asylum
PRT.doc_why: The declaration is what is issued immediately after registration and permits residence and work while the claim is pending; the five-year residence permit is issued on grant of refugee status, while Subsidiary protection status and Temporary Protection Status are status labels with no document name printed
PRT.office: AIMA (Agency for Integration, Migration and Asylum)
PRT.office_why: AIMA both receives and determines applications and Loja AIMA is the branch people actually walk into; the police forces are genuine lodgement points that must notify AIMA within 48 hours, so they are kept as backups rather than dropped

PRY.caveat: Step 2 of the procedure is done by email to CONARE, so v1 asking whether the person went to an office describes only the first step and must be adapted. Two variant names for the asylum-seeker certificate are printed - Constancia de solicitante de refugio and Constancia de Solicitud de Refugio - and it is not clear which respondents use. The carnet de admisión temporaria reads as a residence card and may not be linked to refugee status when heard aloud. No Guaraní wording is printed anywhere despite widespread use
PRY.channel: in person in Asuncion at the Secretaría Ejecutiva de la CONARE, or at Dirección Nacional de Migraciones delegations outside Asuncion or with the migration authority at borders and airports; the application is then FORMALISED BY EMAIL to CONARE with the completed form and identity documents
PRY.doc_alt: Constancia de Solicitud de Refugio, the variant name printed on the Paraguay landing page
PRY.doc_why: The constancia is issued to the applicant on lodging the claim, is free and is valid 2 years renewable, and the carnet de admisión temporaria is obtained after recognition as a refugee, whereas the cédula de identidad civil is the national ID card and the documento de viaje is a travel document
office_alt: autoridad migratoria at borders and airports
PRY.office_why: The Executive Secretariat of CONARE is where the claim is lodged in person and CONARE is the acronym people say, while DNM delegations receive the claim outside Asuncion; the email step only formalises the same claim and no other body receives applications

ROU.caveat: No refugee-status document is named, and the asylum-seeker document is a generic English descriptor with no Romanian name, no validity and no issuer detail. The Romanian-language site serves English throughout, so no Romanian terminology was captured at all - the only local-language names in the source are Ukrainian, usable for Ukrainian-speaking respondents only.
ROU.channel: in person at an IGI office or a regional reception centre; at the border or airport to Border Police
ROU.doc_alt: temporary protection permit (Дозвіл на тимчасовий захист)
ROU.doc_why: the temporary identification document is the only thing the source names as issued to asylum seekers; the residence permit and the CNP belong to the temporary-protection track for Ukrainians and are not refugee-status documents
office_alt: Regional Reception Centres for Accommodation and Procedures for Asylum-Seekers
ROU.office_why: IGI both receives and resolves applications and is the body at whose representations temporary protection is registered, so it genuinely is the lodging point; the court that hears appeals is not

RUS.caveat: Local names given verbatim in Cyrillic as printed in source. Temporary asylum is by far the more commonly granted form, so its two documents matter more in practice than the refugee-status pair: the temporary-asylum свидетельство о предоставлении временного убежища is given as doc_backup and the parallel справка о рассмотрении заявления о предоставлении временного убежища is the temporary-asylum applicant document. A second refugee-track document, свидетельство о рассмотрении ходатайства по существу, is issued once the claim is admitted on the merits. The MOI office is the general interior-ministry office, not a dedicated asylum office, which may weaken recognition of the name.
RUS.channel: in person at the territorial branch of the Ministry of the Interior for the place of stay; refugees must return there to re-register every 18 months
RUS.doc_pending_local: справка о приеме ходатайства о признании беженцем
RUS.doc_why: the справка is handed over on submitting the refugee-status application and the удостоверение беженца is issued on recognition; the contrast between a справка (a receipt slip) and a свидетельство (a certificate) is itself colloquially meaningful in Russian
office_alt: Ministry of the Interior (MOI) of the Russian Federation
территориальный орган МВД России по месту пребывания
RUS.office_why: the MOI territorial office is the counter where applications are lodged in person and where people re-register; UNHCR Russia states verbatim that it does not consider asylum applications there, so it must not be named

RWA.caveat: Applicants outside Kigali lodge the claim with the village leader (umudugudu) and never attend any office, so v1 naming only the immigration department would return false negatives for them - the village leader must be offered as an alternative. The Refugee ID has two distinct Kinyarwanda renderings in the source, Indangamuntu y'impunzi on the documentation page and ikarita iranga impunzi on the Kinyarwanda asylum procedure page, so both should be piloted. Refugee IDs are issued only from age 16, and camp residents register at Mahama, Nyabiheke, Kigeme, Kiziba or Mugombwa camp. MINEMA succeeded MIDIMAR, which older respondents may still name
RWA.channel: in person - written application in 2 copies to DGIE at Kacyiru in Kigali, or lodged with the village leader (umukuru w'umudugudu) outside Kigali; refugee ID applications are taken at the MINEMA Kigali office and in the camps
RWA.doc_alt: Proof of Registration (PoR) issued by UNHCR
RWA.doc_why: the TRP is issued for 3 months while the claim is pending and the Refugee ID on recognition, whereas the decision letter, the Convention Travel Document, the passport and the civil-status certificates (birth, marriage, divorce, death) are not protection documents
RWA.office: Ministry in Charge of Emergency Management (MINEMA)
office_alt: Directorate General of Immigration and Emigration (DGIE)
RWA.office_why: MINEMA is the acronym people say and the office where refugee registration and ID applications are taken in Kigali and in the camps, and DGIE is where the written claim is lodged, whereas the Refugee Appeals Tribunal and the High Court only hear appeals and NIDA only captures biometrics and prints the card

SAU.caveat: v1 needs rewording: registration requests are made by phone or email and the Riyadh office is open to visitors only two days a week, so many respondents will never have attended an office. The single office in Riyadh covers Saudi Arabia, Bahrain, Qatar and Oman, so respondents outside Riyadh will have registered remotely. Both document fields are empty by necessity. The Arabic name in org_best_local is the full printed office name; respondents are far more likely to recognise the short form of the UNHCR name, which is not printed on these pages.
SAU.channel: by phone or email - the Arabic page states that registration requests are made through these channels; in-person visits to the Riyadh office are Monday and Wednesday 09:00-15:00 and the phone line 009668001000281 runs Sunday, Tuesday and Thursday 12:00-16:00
SAU.doc_why: no asylum-seeker or refugee document, card, certificate or validity period is named anywhere in the source, so v2 cannot be worded for Saudi Arabia
office_alt: UNHCR for the GCC States in Riyadh
SAU.office_local: المفوضية السامية للأمم المتحدة لشؤون اللاجئين لدى دول مجلس التعاون الخليجي في الرياض
SAU.office_why: UNHCR is the only registration point named for the country and no Saudi government office, asylum application or procedure appears anywhere on the pages fetched, so there is no government alternative to weigh it against

SDN.caveat: v2 cannot be worded for Sudan without inventing a document name; the contacts page instead tells people to have their individual or household registration number ready, which points to a number rather than a named card. Named places a respondent may give instead of COR include Shagarab camp and Girba (Kassala), the Joda reception centre (White Nile), and the COR offices at Port Sudan (Transit / العبور district) and Wadi Halfa. who_registers is set to BOTH because registration in Sudan is joint, but only COR is printed as registering, so a reviewer may prefer GOVERNMENT.
SDN.channel: in person at a COR office or at the camps and reception centres; UNHCR itself is reached by hotline (Zain 0900934474, Sudani 123184860, interagency toll-free 1460) or WhatsApp rather than by visiting an office
SDN.doc_why: no protection document is named anywhere on the Sudan pages: the only named documents are civil (birth certificate, marriage certificate, national ID card) and the protection wording printed is generic (refugee or asylum seeker document, temporary documents), which is descriptive phrasing rather than a product name
SDN.office_why: COR is the body printed as carrying out refugee and asylum-seeker registration and document reissuance, and COR is the acronym people say, whereas UNHCR appears on the same pages only through hotline and WhatsApp numbers, which are contact channels and not a place people attended

SEN.caveat: No French name is printed for the refugee identity card, so doc_refugee must be read out in English or verified before fielding in French or Wolof - the Carte de réfugié on the FAQ is a different thing and must not be substituted. The refugee identity card is described as equivalent to a residence permit, so respondents may describe it as a residence document rather than a protection document. The police interview at the Cite de la Police is a step a question naming only an immigration or refugee office would miss.
SEN.channel: in person at the CNE in Dakar (Immeuble Serigne Saliou Mbacke, Bd du President Habib Bourguiba) - the form, a letter and four identity photos are handed to the NEC Secretariat; a second interview is held by a police inspector at the Cite de la Police, Place Washington
SEN.doc_alt: certificate issued by the NEC while awaiting presidential confirmation ; document valable pendant deux mois issued after a second-instance rejection
SEN.doc_why: the récépissé is what the CNE issues on filing, is valid 6 months renewable and permits free circulation, so it is the registration product respondents will name; the certificate and the two-month document are interim papers tied to specific later stages, and the Carte de réfugié printed on the FAQ refers to a card issued by another country so it is deliberately not used as the French name of the refugee identity card
office_alt: Cité de la Police, Place Washington, Dakar
SEN.office_why: the CNE is printed verbatim as the sole body where asylum applications are filed and its Secretariat physically receives the form, letter and four photos, so it registers as well as assesses; the President of the Republic only confirms recognition on appeal, and BOS and the Green Village Foundation are UNHCR partner offices offering assistance rather than registration

SLB.caveat: Genuinely thin data rather than a confirmed absence - nothing has been published rather than nothing existing. help.unhcr.org/pacific carries no country-specific text and directs people to the UNHCR Representation outside the country (Canberra), so neither version of the question can be fielded without new country research
SLB.doc_why: no permit, certificate or card is named in any source for the Solomon Islands
SLB.office_why: no asylum authority or office of any kind is named: RIMAP node 166 lists asylum-category legal instruments only and its country context page is marked Content to be added

SLV.caveat: Accents were stripped at extraction for TSV safety and should be restored before fielding (Comisión, Determinación, Migración, Atención, República). Spanish-only source, so no English document name exists and the local fields repeat the Spanish name. Validity discrepancy in the source: the asylum-seeker carnet is given as treinta dias renovables on one page and 6 meses on the renewal page. CODER sits inside the Ministerio de Relaciones Exteriores building with no dedicated walk-in asylum counter named, so people may describe going to la Cancilleria
SLV.channel: in person at the Foreign Ministry or at CAIPEM; CODER also reachable by phone and e-mail
SLV.doc_recognised: carnet de Permanencia Temporal Especial en calidad de refugiado con permiso de trabajo
SLV.doc_recognised_local: carnet de Permanencia Temporal Especial en calidad de refugiado con permiso de trabajo
SLV.doc_why: both documents are issued by the protection procedure itself - the provisional carnet on lodging and the special temporary residence carnet on recognition - and respondents call both simply el carnet, which is the wording worth testing
SLV.office_local: Comision para la Determinacion de la Condicion de Personas Refugiadas
SLV.office_why: applications are lodged with CODER even though it also decides, and CODER is the acronym people say; DGME is only the general immigration authority at the airport and border and the Procuraduria General de la Republica only provides legal representation

SOM.caveat: The organization must be swapped by region - NCRI for South-Central, NDRA for Somaliland, HPD-MoIFAD for Puntland - so one national name will misfire in two of the three zones. RIMAP states recognised refugees receive identity documentation but prints no refugee document name, so doc_refugee is genuinely absent rather than overlooked. Yemeni nationals (and in Somaliland Afghans, Syrians and Palestinians) get prima facie status
SOM.channel: in person at the regional registration office
SOM.doc_why: the Asylum Seeker Certificate is what registration produces and it carries a verbatim Somali name people can be asked about; Proof of Registration (Caddaynta Diiwaangelinta) is the individual-level slip issued at the same moment and is the backup; no document name is printed for recognised refugees
SOM.office: National Commission for Refugees and IDPs (NCRI)
office_alt: Human Protection Department of the Ministry of Interior, Federal Affair and Democratization (HPD-MoIFAD)
SOM.office_why: NCRI is the registration body for Southern and Central Somalia where most of the caseload is; NDRA and HPD-MoIFAD are the equivalent registrars in Somaliland and Puntland and must replace it there

SRB.caveat: help.unhcr.org Serbia publishes no Serbian-language version, so the only local-script wording in the source is the Asylum Office mailing address line (Ministarstvo unutrašnjih poslova, Uprava granične policije, Kancelarija za azil); all document names are English only and Serbian wording must be verified before fielding. The certificate the police issue at the first step is described on the help page only as a certificate in the Serbian language, its formal title coming from the 2018 Rulebook. No IDP document or registering body is named despite 209,704 IDPs recorded
SRB.channel: in person - the Border Police first registers the intention to seek asylum and issues the registration certificate, and the asylum application is then lodged with the Asylum Office; in Belgrade travel-document appointments are arranged with the Asylum Office by email
SRB.doc_alt: Certificate on Registration of a Foreigner Who Expressed Intention to Seek Asylum, issued by the police at the first step; ID Card for Subsidiary Protection
SRB.doc_why: The asylum-seeker's ID card is the personal document issued to applicants during the procedure and the Refugee ID Card follows the grant of refugee status, whereas the travel documents are excluded, the Personal Number and the Certificate on EBS are registration identifiers rather than documents, and the Asylum Application Form is a form
office_alt: Border Police (registers the intention to seek asylum)
Serbian Commissariat for Refugees and Migration (KIRS)
SRB.office_why: The Asylum Office receives asylum applications and conducts the interviews, and the Border Police performs the prior registration of the intention to seek asylum, whereas KIRS only manages accommodation and reception centres and the municipal trustee is a local contact point rather than a registration body

SSD.caveat: No local-language names exist for South Sudan: the Arabic, French, Amharic and Tigrinya mirrors all served English content. Registration is biometric (BIMS). CRA is never expanded on the registration page itself.
SSD.channel: in person at the reception centre or protection desk of the nearest UNHCR office
SSD.doc_why: Both are named verbatim as documents issued jointly by UNHCR and CRA on registration and on recognition; the generic phrase ID documentation is excluded because no product name is printed for it
SSD.office_why: The printed instruction sends applicants to the UNHCR reception centre or protection desk; CRA co-registers but is printed only as a bare acronym with no office address, so UNHCR is the name a respondent would recognise

SUR.caveat: Neither version works unchanged: there has been no office in the country since 31 March 2025 and no protection document is named, so doc fields are left empty rather than filled with the generic residence permit; respondents who registered before the closure will name ACNUR, and people arriving since may have registered with nobody
SUR.channel: no office to visit - UNHCR closed its Suriname office on 31 March 2025, all registration processes were cancelled and no new appointments are scheduled; registration and RSD are run remotely from the UNHCR Regional Office in Washington DC and the only contact point is a web form
SUR.doc_why: No asylum-seeker or refugee document is named on the source; the only document printed is a generic permiso de residencia with no issuing office, validity period or application point, so it cannot carry a protection question
office_alt: UNHCR Regional Office based in Washington DC
SUR.office_why: UNHCR is the only body named as conducting registration and refugee status determination in Suriname; no Surinamese government asylum body appears anywhere on the source, which refers only to el estado donde busca asilo o el ACNUR

SVK.caveat: No Slovak name is printed for either residence permit and both sound generic, so respondents may not link them to protection status. The physical temporary protection document has no printed title on either language version - the Certificate of Stay (Potvrdenie o zotrvaní) is the nearest named document. Temporary protection cannot be applied for without first completing the online pre-registration form and booking, so that pathway is online-then-office and most Foreign Police departments process it on Thursdays only
SVK.channel: in person - the claim is lodged at a border crossing, transit zone, police station, detention centre or prison and registration follows at a reception camp (záchytný tábor); temporary protection requires an online pre-registration form and an appointment booked through the rezervačný systém before attending the Foreigners Police
SVK.doc_why: the registration card is issued at the reception camp as a direct result of registering and the permanent residence permit is granted on being given asylum, whereas the Declaration of the Foreigner and the Asylum Application Questionnaire are forms filled in during the procedure rather than documents kept, and subsidiary protection holders receive a temporary residence permit instead
SVK.office: Migration Office of the Ministry of Interior of the Slovak Republic
office_alt: Office of the Border and Aliens Police (Úrad hraničnej a cudzineckej polície)
SVK.office_local: Migračný úrad Ministerstva vnútra Slovenskej republiky (Migračný úrad)
SVK.office_why: Migračný úrad is the competent asylum authority and the short Slovak name people use, the Border and Aliens Police is where the claim is physically lodged and the Foreigners Police is where Ukrainians register temporary protection, whereas the District Office is a general local-government office and the Points of Safety are support and integration centres, not registration points

SVN.caveat: Key misfire case for v1 - there is no asylum office, so the organization slot is filled by the police station and the wording must be rebuilt for this country. No Slovenian-language names are printed for any office or document, and no card is named for recognised refugees or for temporary protection beneficiaries
SVN.channel: at any police station, at the border on entry, or to any state or local authority - no asylum office to visit
SVN.doc_alt: asylum-seeker card; a document confirming that you have asked for international protection
SVN.doc_why: The asylum applicant card is the card issued after registration and asylum-seeker card is a printed variant of the same thing; the confirmation document is only an interim slip held until the card arrives, and no document is named for recognised refugees
office_alt: Government Office for the Support and Integration of Migrants (GOSIM/UOIM)
SVN.office_why: The intention to seek international protection is expressed at any police station, at the border or to any state or local authority - there is no asylum or migration office at that stage; the Ministry of the Interior only decides the application and the Administrative Court only hears appeals

SWE.caveat: Swedish spelling LMA-kort is not printed in the source so the local field is left empty. Temporary protection is applied for through the Migrationsverket website with no office visit, so v1 misfires for the Ukrainian caseload. The refugee document is a generic residence permit card with no distinct name.
SWE.channel: in person at a Migration Agency office, no appointment needed; temporary protection for Ukrainians is applied for online only
SWE.doc_why: The LMA card is described verbatim as the certificate that you are an asylum-seeker, issued after registration; AT-UND is excluded as a work-permit exemption and the personal identity number as a population-register number
SWE.office_why: Migrationsverket receives and registers asylum applications on a walk-in basis; the Migration Court and Migration Court of Appeal are appeal instances, the Tax Agency handles population registration, and the Swedish Refugee Law Center is a legal-aid partner

SXM.caveat: Major misfire case. The only channel given is email, followed up by UNHCR, so v1 as worded cannot be used and v2 cannot be worded at all. UNHCR is the correct answer for who registers, but there is no place a respondent could say they went to.
SXM.channel: by email to UNHCR; no in-country office named
SXM.doc_why: No document is named for Sint Maarten, so v2 cannot be worded
SXM.office_why: The country is routed to UNHCR rather than to the state, so UNHCR and not a national authority processes asylum claims; no national asylum office and no in-country UNHCR office is named

SYR.caveat: No Arabic name is printed for the refugee card. Syria has no national asylum authority, no asylum-specific legislation and is not a party to the 1951 Convention, so naming a government body here would be wrong.
SYR.channel: in person at a UNHCR registration centre, by appointment made by contacting the nearest UNHCR office
SYR.doc_why: Both are named verbatim as what UNHCR issues on registration and on recognition; no other document is named for Syria
office_alt: UNHCR registration centre (Damascus, Aleppo, Tartous, Homs, Qamishli)
SYR.office_why: UNHCR is the registrar under its mandate in Syria; the RSD unit is excluded because it decides claims rather than receiving them, and the General Directorate of Civil Affairs plays no part in asylum registration

TCA.caveat: The source names no government office, department, document, validity period or legal basis for the territory; the same email instruction covers the Cayman Islands, Jamaica, Montserrat and Turks and Caicos Islands together. Both v1 and v2 misfire.
TCA.channel: by email, no office in country
TCA.doc_why: no document is named in the source
TCA.office_why: the only instruction given is to email UNHCR; no government office or department is named for the territory, so there is no lodgement place to name

THA.caveat: No Thai-language mirror was found, so no local-language names are available and the prompts would have to be translated by the interviewer. No document is named for Protected Person status under the government NSM, so someone screened by the NSM rather than registered by UNHCR would recognise neither card name. The first registration step is an online portal request, so v1 misfires for it.
THA.channel: UNHCR registration starts online through the My Services Portal and is followed by an appointment at the UNHCR Office in Bangkok, with drop-in card renewal on Wednesdays and Thursdays; the source warns of a wait of up to two years to be registered; the parallel government NSM route is lodged in person at Sub-Division 4 of the Immigration Bureau at Bangkhen
THA.doc_why: the asylum-seeker card and the refugee card are the two variants of the UNHCR Thailand Card, issued on registration and on recognition respectively; both are commonly called simply the UNHCR card, which is the form to say aloud
THA.office_why: UNHCR is the body that registers and issues the card in Thailand, so it is where a respondent actually went; the NSM is the parallel government screening route named on the same page and Sub-Division 4 of the Immigration Bureau is where an NSM applicant physically applies, while Asylum Access, the Center for Asylum Protection, JRS, Peace Rights Foundation and Tzu Chi are legal aid and service NGOs that do not register anyone

TJK.caveat: DCWR sits inside the interior-ministry passport service, so respondents may report going to the police or the passport office rather than an asylum office and a v1 stem naming DCWR alone may be under-recognised. Only Russian names are printed; no Tajik-language names.
TJK.channel: in person at the DCWR office of the Passport Registration Service; no online, email or appointment channel is named
TJK.doc_why: These are the only two documents named and they map exactly onto registration (3 months, renewable) and recognition; no other candidate exists in the source
TJK.office: Department on Citizenship and Work with Refugees (DCWR)
office_alt: Passport Registration Service of the Ministry of Internal Affairs
TJK.office_local: Отдел гражданства и работы с беженцами
TJK.office_why: DCWR is the primary asylum authority where claims are lodged; the joint standing commission is excluded as the RSD decision body, NGO Inson va Adolat as a legal-aid partner, and UNHCR because it explicitly does not register or issue documents in Central Asia

TKM.caveat: The source states no asylum-seeker has been registered by the authorities since 2009, so in practice neither the SMS registration nor the temporary certificate will be recognised by respondents - treat a positive answer with care. UNHCR has no in-country office, so v1 wording misfires for the UNHCR route. Local names are Russian; no Turkmen-language names printed.
TKM.channel: in person at a State Migration Service office; UNHCR has no office in the country and counsels by email and hotline from Almaty
TKM.doc_why: these are the only two status documents named; the travel document for international travel is excluded as a travel document
TKM.office_why: the source states verbatim that the SMS registers asylum-seekers and determines refugee status; Keik Okara is a legal-aid NGO and the only in-country walk-in point named, but it does not register

TON.caveat: Total data gap. RIMAP node 182 carries only a constitutional asylum provision with no dedicated refugee or asylum statute, no authority, office, permit or document; country context reads Content to be added and help.unhcr.org covers Tonga only through a regional Pacific page. who_registers is recorded as NONE because the source names no registrar, not because none exists - a Pacific regional check is needed before fielding.
TON.doc_why: no permit, certificate or document is named for Tonga in the source
TON.office_why: no authority, office, reception point or body of any kind is named for Tonga in the source, so no organization can be chosen without inventing one

TTO.caveat: who_registers is NONE because nobody registers asylum claims in country today, but for a lifetime-recall question UNHCR is the correct name to say: it registered until the office closed on 31 August 2025 and has stated it is no longer conducting RSD, scheduling interviews or issuing decisions. v1 must not imply a place to visit. Named partners (Caribbean Centre for Human Rights, La Casita) are referral NGOs, not registrars.
TTO.channel: no office in country; by email to the UNHCR Multi-Country Office in Panama since the UNHCR office closed on 31 August 2025
TTO.doc_why: No asylum-seeker or refugee document is named anywhere in source for Trinidad and Tobago, so v2 cannot be worded here; the only card named, the Migrant Registration Card, is a general regularisation open to every undocumented migrant regardless of nationality or protection need and must not be used
TTO.office_why: UNHCR was the only body that ever registered asylum claims here and is the name any past applicant would recognise; the Refugee Unit within the Immigration Division is only foreseen in policy and not confirmed as operating, and the Ministry of Homeland Security runs a general migrant registration, not an asylum procedure

TUR.caveat: Non-Europeans cannot obtain refugee status in Turkiye, so the refugee column holds the temporary protection card (Kimlik) that Syrians receive; UNHCR ended registration and mandate RSD on 10 September 2018, so respondents who arrived before then may recall registering with UNHCR instead. Most Syrian respondents will use the Arabic name held in doc_backup
TUR.doc_alt: بطاقة هوية الحماية المؤقتة (Arabic name of the Temporary Protection Identification Card)
TUR.doc_pending_local: Uluslararası Koruma Başvuru Sahibi Kimlik Belgesi
TUR.doc_why: Both cards are issued as a direct result of PDMM registration; the Foreigner ID Number (99 xxxxxx) is a number printed on those cards, not a separate document
office_alt: Presidency of Migration Management (Göç İdaresi Başkanlığı)
TUR.office_why: PDMM is the office printed as the place where both Syrians and non-Syrians actually register, whereas the Presidency only makes the final assessment, IPEC only hears appeals and 157 YIMER is a telephone line

TUV.caveat: Nothing usable for either question version. Source carries only a constitutional provision under the asylum-rights category and the country context page states Content to be added. Both v1 and v2 need original field research or a regional Pacific source before this country can be worded.
TUV.doc_why: No permit, certificate or document name is printed in any source for this country
TUV.office_why: No asylum authority, office or registration body is named in any source; only a constitutional asylum-rights provision exists, with no dedicated refugee or asylum statute

UGA.caveat: No colloquial or colour name is printed for any Uganda document and the site is English-only. UNHCR sub-offices and field offices are listed extensively but are never described as registration points, so who_registers is recorded as GOVERNMENT even though UNHCR supports the REC. Those in settlements report to the Settlement Commandant rather than to a Kampala office.
UGA.channel: in person at the office, at a settlement reception centre, or at a border checkpoint
UGA.doc_why: the attestation is what OPM issues on registration and the identification document on recognition; the CTD is a travel document and is excluded, and the Reference Card is issued earlier at the Refugee Desk on the first request
UGA.office_why: OPM is named as the body that registers asylum seekers and issues the attestation, while the Refugee Eligibility Committee and the Refugee Appeals Board only process and decide claims

UKR.caveat: No refugee-status or complementary-protection document is named anywhere in the source, so doc_refugee is empty. The Cyrillic form of the asylum seeker certificate is not printed (only the transliteration dovidka), and the formal name of the IDP registration certificate is a flagged coverage gap. Keep the displacement track (Довідка ВПО, evacuation documents) strictly separate from the refugee track when wording the item.
UKR.channel: in person at a State Migration Service office; IDP registration is done separately with local authorities
UKR.doc_why: the asylum seeker certificate is what the SMS is stated to issue on registering the claim; the IDP certificate belongs to the internal-displacement track and must never be offered as an international-protection document
office_alt: local authorities (органах місцевої влади) - IDP registration only
UKR.office_why: the State Migration Service registers the application, determines identity and issues the certificate; the SMS central office in Kyiv only makes the final determination, and the Bureau of Legal Aid and the Diia app are not registration channels

URY.caveat: v1 needs rewording: there is no single office, the lodging point differs between Montevideo and the interior, and the decisive formalisation step is an email to SPCORE. Recognised refugees receive residencia permanente and the ordinary cédula, so Uruguay has no refugee-specific document to name in v2. A reviewer who prefers maximum recognition over the registrar/adjudicator distinction should consider CORE as the stem, since applicants deal with it throughout.
URY.channel: MIXED - the claim is first lodged verbally or in writing in person (Ministerio de Relaciones Exteriores, SEDHU or the Centro de Referencia a Migrantes in Montevideo, the nearest Direccion Nacional de Migracion elsewhere, or the autoridad migratoria at a border or airport), then formalised BY EMAIL to the Secretaria Permanente de la CORE; the Certificado Migratorio is processed online at GOB.UY
URY.doc_alt: Cédula de Identidad Provisoria, 2 años, issued to asylum seekers by DNIC ; Cédula de Identidad Civil issued to recognised refugees ; Certificado Migratorio, processed online at GOB.UY
URY.doc_why: the Constancia is issued free by CORE and acredita el inicio de tu tramite, so it is the direct product of lodging the claim; the Cédula de Identidad Civil that recognised refugees receive is the ordinary Uruguayan national identity card that every resident holds and would produce false positives, the Documento de viaje is a travel document and the Certificado Migratorio is an online migration certificate, so the refugee slot is left empty
office_alt: Servicio Ecuménico para la Dignidad Humana (SEDHU)
URY.office_why: DNM is the in-person government migration office printed as the lodging point and is the name respondents everywhere recognise, whereas the CORE is the status determination body and its Secretaria Permanente receives the formalisation only by email so neither is an office anyone attended; SEDHU and the Centro de Referencia a Migrantes are the Montevideo lodging points and Abitab is a commercial payment network, not a government office

USA.caveat: Source explicitly records that no asylum-seeker ID card or receipt notice appears on any page, and that Form I-94 and the Employment Authorization Document / EAD are NOT printed and must not be introduced. v1 cannot be used unchanged: there is no office to attend. The green card is named but is lawful permanent resident status applied for a year after an asylum grant, not the protection document; I-730, I-590, AOR and P-2/P-3 are resettlement and family reunification items.
USA.channel: by form submitted to USCIS with no office to attend (post or online not stated in source); defensive claims are heard in Immigration Court by summons
USA.doc_alt: Form I-589, Application for Asylum and for Withholding of Removal
USA.doc_why: no asylum-seeker or refugee document is named anywhere in the source, only the I-589 application form, which is what a person fills in rather than what they are issued, so both document fields are left empty
USA.office_why: USCIS is the body the affirmative application is submitted to, but the source describes no counter to attend; EOIR, the Immigration Court, the BIA and the federal courts only adjudicate, and Immigration Court attendance is by hearing summons rather than walk-in registration

UZB.caveat: Both versions of the question are unusable here and the empty cells are a confirmed absence, not thin data - the page states verbatim that Uzbekistan has not acceded to the 1951 Convention or the 1967 Protocol and has no national asylum system. RIMAP nonetheless records 8,005 refugees, so respondents may still self-identify; any wording will have to describe the situation rather than name an office or a document
UZB.channel: no office in country; remote counselling only by hotline, WhatsApp, Telegram or email
UZB.doc_why: no asylum-seeker or refugee document exists to name: the source states people seeking international protection in Uzbekistan cannot apply for asylum or obtain refugee status
UZB.office_why: no organization qualifies: the page states there is no national asylum system and that UNHCR has no representation in Uzbekistan and does not register refugees, so the Representation to Central Asia in Almaty (УВКБ ООН) counsels only and is not a place anyone registered

VCT.caveat: Major misfire case for both versions. There is no office a respondent could say they went to - the only channel is email and the registrar is an honorary liaison working through an unnamed local partner - so v1 needs bespoke wording. No asylum-seeker or refugee document is named, so v2 cannot be worded from this source
VCT.channel: by email to UNHCR, followed up by the UNHCR Honorary Liaison through a local partner; no office in country
VCT.doc_alt: Temporary identity documentation (discretionary, issued at the discretion of immigration authorities)
VCT.doc_why: the only document named is discretionary temporary identity documentation issued by general immigration authorities and printed in the statelessness rather than the refugee context, so it is not issued as a result of registering for protection and is kept only as a backup
VCT.office_why: the country is routed to UNHCR rather than to the state, and registration and status determination are carried out by the UNHCR Honorary Liaison through a local partner with regional offices taking the final decision; no national asylum office and no in-country UNHCR office is named

VEN.caveat: The document version of the question cannot be fielded: the Venezuela entry carries office rows only, so both document columns are empty by necessity, not omission. The organization side is usable and CONARE is the name in everyday use on the help site, though the law abbreviates the framework as LORRAA. Regional Defensoría offices exist in Amazonas, Caracas, Apure, Bolivar, Tachira and Zulia and may be recalled by respondents who sought help there, but they are not registration points
VEN.channel: in person at a CONARE office - Caracas (Av. Universidad, esquina de San Francisco, Centro Mercantil), Tachira, Apure or Zulia
VEN.doc_why: No asylum-seeker or refugee document is named anywhere in the source - SAIME is described only as providing debida identificacion to recognised refugees, without naming the document it issues
office_alt: Servicio Administrativo de Identificación, Migración y Extranjería (SAIME)
VEN.office_why: CONARE is the only body printed with street addresses and in-person lodging, so it is where people actually go rather than only the deciding commission, whereas SAIME only issues identification after recognition and the Defensoría del Pueblo is an ombudsman the source explicitly describes as not a registration office

VGB.caveat: Same Caribbean routing note as Antigua and Barbuda is the only source content available - the only channel named is email, no office exists to visit and no document is named. Both versions need bespoke wording
VGB.channel: by email to UNHCR; no office in country
VGB.doc_why: No document of any kind is named for asylum seekers or recognised refugees, so v2 cannot be worded for this country
VGB.office_why: UNHCR and not the state processes asylum claims here; no national asylum authority and no in-country office of any kind is named in the source

VUT.caveat: Nothing is named, so v2 cannot be worded and v1 can only say UNHCR; the source note is cut off at directs people to the UNHCR Rep, so the full name of that office - a regional representation outside the country - is not recorded and must not be invented
VUT.channel: no office in the country; help.unhcr.org/pacific gives no country-specific text and directs people to the UNHCR representation covering the region
VUT.doc_why: No permit, card, certificate or document name is printed for Vanuatu on either source
VUT.office_why: No asylum authority, office or registration point is named on RIMAP or on help.unhcr.org - the country context page states Content to be added and the Pacific page only directs people to UNHCR, so UNHCR is the only body that can be named

WSM.caveat: No usable data - RIMAP lists only a constitutional provision with no dedicated refugee or asylum statute, and no authority, office, permit or document is named. who_registers is recorded as NONE to reflect the absence of any named body in the source, which is not evidence that no procedure exists. Neither v1 nor v2 can be worded from this source
WSM.doc_why: No permit or document name is printed in the source
WSM.office_why: No authority, office or body of any kind is named in the source - only a constitutional provision is listed and the country context page states content is to be added

XCA.caveat: This is a regional catch-all covering 18 territories with no per-country offices or documents named, so anything here is generic and should be replaced by country-specific wording wherever it exists. Kreyol forms printed with accents in source, stripped here for TSV safety. Useful terminology for wording: demande dazil for asylum seeker, refijiye for refugee. Registration is by email only, so v1 cannot be used unchanged. Dominican Republic is routed off this site and captured separately.
XCA.channel: by email only; no office in country, the region is served remotely from the UNHCR Panama office
XCA.doc_why: the refugee certificate is the only document named anywhere on the regional site; the Kreyol page separately names an asylum-seeker certificate that the English page does not, which is the only asylum-seeker document available for this entry
XCA.office_why: UNHCR is the registrar across the UNHCR-route territories of the region; no national asylum office is named anywhere on the regional site, so there is no government body to offer

XPA.caveat: Regional page only, with no per-country detail for Cook Islands, Federated States of Micronesia, Fiji, Kiribati, Marshall Islands or the other covered states, whose national systems differ. The responsible office is in Australia and no in-region contact point is printed, so v1 cannot be asked as written - a respondent in the Pacific did not go to any office - and v2 cannot be asked at all. The source states UNHCR Canberra is responsible for the promotion and protection of refugee rights but does not state that UNHCR registers claims, so who_registers is inferred and weak. Country-level source work is needed before fielding.
XPA.channel: no office in the region - the only channels printed are the emergency protection line +61 408 619 052 and email aulca@unhcr.org to the UNHCR Representation in Canberra, Australia
XPA.doc_why: No document, certificate or card of any kind is named for any of the 14 Pacific states
XPA.office_why: UNHCR Canberra is the only body named for the region and no government office, department or authority is named for any of the 14 Pacific states covered

YEM.caveat: Registration body varies by nationality and city (IPNA/BRA in Sana, UNHCR in Aden for non-Somalis, IPNA for Somalis in Aden), so a single organization name in the question stem will misfire for part of the population. Somalis receive prima facie refugee status but no refugee document name is printed. No Arabic-script names were captured. Certificate valid 1 year and must be renewed
YEM.channel: in person at a registration centre; non-Somalis in Aden first contact UNHCR by phone, SMS or WhatsApp
YEM.doc_why: the asylum-seeker certificate is the only protection document named and is issued on registration; the Identity Attestation Form and Medical Test Form are inputs required before registering, not outcomes, and no document is named for recognised refugees
YEM.office_why: IPNA is the authority that actually registers claims in both Sana and Aden and runs the named registration centres; BRA is the counter inside the IPNA compound in Sana and UNHCR registers only non-Somalis in Aden

ZAF.caveat: Five Refugee Reception Offices are named: Cape Town, Desmond Tutu (Pretoria), Durban, Gqeberha and Musina. Gqeberha was formerly Port Elizabeth and respondents recalling older events will say Port Elizabeth. Renewals moved to email, so v1 misfires for anyone whose only recent contact was a renewal, and respondents may name the RSDO who interviewed them rather than the office. Source prints Department for Home Affairs; the correct title Department of Home Affairs is used here.
ZAF.channel: in person at a Refugee Reception Office for the initial claim, with no online portal; extensions and renewals are requested by email to the RRO where the person last renewed, with the permit number in the subject line, and family joining is also by email, so those steps involve no visit
ZAF.doc_why: section 22 is issued on lodging the claim and section 24 is the written recognition of refugee status, which is exactly the two-step pair the question needs; the refugee travel document is excluded as a travel document and the Refugee ID is held as a backup because it is issued alongside recognition rather than being the recognition itself
ZAF.office_why: the RRO is the physical place an applicant must attend to lodge an initial claim and the source states no online portal exists for it; Home Affairs is what people say in speech and is the fallback prompt for anyone who cannot recall the office name, while the Refugee Appeals Authority, the Standing Committee for Refugee Affairs and the RSDO are excluded because they decide rather than register
